modules.title: Tenant setup, domains, health, users, groups and licensing
learningObjectives: Create a tenant and add and verify a custom domain, including all service DNS records.
Configure organisation settings, Security & privacy and the Organization profile.
Use Service health, Message center, Network connectivity and Adoption Score to run the tenant proactively.
Control Microsoft 365 Apps update channels and understand Microsoft 365 Backup.
Create users, guests, contacts, groups and shared mailboxes and manage licences with group-based licensing and Microsoft Graph PowerShell.
modules.executiveSummary:
Every Microsoft 365 engagement starts with the **tenant**: the Microsoft Entra directory plus the subscriptions attached to it. The tenant is created with an initial `*.onmicrosoft.com` domain that can never be removed, so production identities should use a **verified custom domain**.

This module covers the day-1 and day-2 tasks of a tenant administrator: domains and DNS, organisation-wide settings, monitoring (Service health, Message center, Network connectivity, Adoption Score), Microsoft 365 Apps update control, **Microsoft 365 Backup**, and the identity objects the exam expects you to manage - users, guests, contacts, groups, shared mailboxes and licences.

For an MSP, getting this right once and documenting it as a **standard tenant baseline** is what makes 30 small customers manageable by an 8-person team.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: The `<name>.onmicrosoft.com` domain created with the tenant.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Guarantees every tenant has a routable namespace before custom domains are verified; it cannot be deleted, so pick the tenant name carefully.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: A TXT record (MS=msXXXXXXXX), or an MX record with a high priority value, or a text file on the website that proves domain ownership.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Prevents one tenant from claiming a domain it does not own.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: MX, Autodiscover CNAME, SPF TXT and optional DKIM/DMARC and Teams records generated by the domain wizard.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Routes mail to Exchange Online Protection and lets clients auto-configure; email authentication protects the domain from spoofing.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Assigning licences to a security, mail-enabled security or Microsoft 365 group so members inherit them.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Removes manual licence work and automatically reclaims licences when people leave the group.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Pay-as-you-go backup of Exchange Online, OneDrive and SharePoint billed through an Azure subscription.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Gives fast, in-boundary restore points for ransomware or mass-deletion recovery beyond recycle bins and retention.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Health > Network connectivity: per-location network assessments and recommendations from Microsoft 365 client telemetry.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Shows when proxies, VPN hair-pinning or distant DNS resolvers degrade Teams/Exchange/SharePoint performance.

modules.deepDive:
### Domains
- Add a domain in **admin.microsoft.com > Settings > Domains > Add domain**. Verify with a TXT record (preferred), an MX record (set a **high priority number** so it does not break existing mail) or a text file uploaded to the website root.
- After verification add the service records: **MX** pointing to `<domain-with-dashes>.mail.protection.outlook.com`, **Autodiscover CNAME**, **SPF TXT** (`v=spf1 include:spf.protection.outlook.com -all`), plus DKIM selector CNAMEs and a DMARC TXT record for email authentication.
- Registrars that support **Domain Connect** can add records automatically; otherwise add them manually. The verification TXT record can be removed after verification.
- The **default domain** determines the suffix proposed for new users; the onmicrosoft.com domain stays as a fallback.

### Organisation settings
- **Settings > Org settings** has three tabs: **Services** (e.g. Microsoft 365 installation options, Adoption Score), **Security & privacy** (password expiration policy, privacy profile/privacy statement URL, sharing, customer lockbox where licensed) and **Organization profile** (organisation information, release preferences such as Targeted release, custom themes, data location).
- **Release preferences**: Standard release vs Targeted release for everyone or selected users - an MSP typically puts its own staff and one pilot user per customer on targeted release.

### Monitoring
- **Health > Service health** shows incidents and advisories; *Customize > Email* sends notifications to up to two email addresses per admin. Planned maintenance is **not** shown in Service health - it appears in **Message center** (filter *Plan for change*).
- **Health > Network connectivity** needs office locations (auto-detected or entered with egress IP ranges). The Service Support Administrator role configures locations; Report Reader can view.
- **Reports > Adoption Score** measures people experiences (communication, meetings, content collaboration, teamwork, mobility, AI adoption). Privacy controls in *Org settings > Adoption Score* allow excluding groups or opting out.

### Software updates
- For users who self-install from Office.com, the update channel is set in **Org settings > Services > Microsoft 365 installation options**.
- **Cloud update** in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center (config.office.com) manages channels via profiles (Current, Monthly Enterprise) with rollout waves, exclusion windows, pause and rollback.

### Users, groups and licences
- Users can be cloud-only, synchronized or **external (B2B guests)**. Guests are invited and authenticate at their home tenant.
- **Contacts** (mail contacts) are directory objects with an external email address but no sign-in - ideal for supplier address-book entries.
- Group types: **Microsoft 365 Groups** (shared mailbox, calendar, SharePoint site, Teams), **security groups**, **mail-enabled security groups**, **distribution lists**, and dynamic membership groups (Entra ID P1).
- **Shared mailboxes** do not need a licence for normal use (within size limits); users access them via permissions.
- **Group-based licensing** (admin center: *Billing > Licenses > Assign licenses*) does not process **nested groups**; users without a usage location inherit the tenant location. Errors (not enough licences, conflicting service plans, missing dependencies) appear under *Errors & issues*.
- Bulk work: **Microsoft Graph PowerShell** (`Connect-MgGraph`, `New-MgUser`, `Set-MgUserLicense`, `Set-MgGroupLicense`) or **Microsoft Entra PowerShell**; the legacy MSOnline and AzureAD modules are retired.
modules.architecture:
### How the pieces fit
- **Tenant = Microsoft Entra directory**: every workload (Exchange, SharePoint, Teams, Defender, Purview) reads identities and groups from the same directory.
- **Subscriptions** add service plans; a **licence** assigns service plans to a user. A user without an Exchange plan has no mailbox; removing a licence starts a grace period before data deletion.
- **DNS** is outside Microsoft: Microsoft only *reads* your zone. MX controls inbound mail flow to Exchange Online Protection, Autodiscover drives Outlook profile creation, SPF/DKIM/DMARC are evaluated by receiving servers.
- **Group-based licensing engine** in Entra ID evaluates membership changes and assigns/removes licences asynchronously; processing time grows with group size.
- **Microsoft 365 Backup** uses Microsoft's own storage within the service boundary; billing flows through a linked **Azure subscription, resource group and region** configured in pay-as-you-go setup. Restore can be in place or to a new location, with *express restore points* for fast OneDrive/SharePoint recovery.
- **Network connectivity** consumes telemetry from Office clients, aggregates by egress location and compares latency to other customers in the same city.
modules.realWorldExample:
**Scenario - 60-user engineering firm in Ghent (Belgium)**

The customer moves from a hosted Exchange 2013 to Microsoft 365 Business Premium. As MSP you:
1. Create the tenant `ingbureau-gent.onmicrosoft.com` and add `ingbureau.be` with a **TXT** verification record at the Belgian registrar (no Domain Connect support).
2. Keep the existing MX until the mailbox migration cut-over, then switch MX, Autodiscover and SPF; enable DKIM and publish a DMARC record starting at `p=none` with reports to the MSP mailbox.
3. Create dynamic groups `LIC-BP-Staff` (department not empty) and assign Business Premium through **group-based licensing**; leavers lose their licence automatically when HR disables them.
4. Convert `info@` and `facturatie@` to **shared mailboxes** (no licence) and add supplier contacts as **mail contacts**.
5. Configure Service health email notifications to the MSP NOC mailbox and create two office locations (Ghent HQ, Antwerp site) in **Network connectivity** - which reveals that the Antwerp VPN backhauls Teams traffic.
6. Offer **Microsoft 365 Backup** as a managed add-on for the CAD project SharePoint sites, billed through the customer's Azure subscription.
examTips: If a registrar cannot create TXT records, verify with an MX record that has a high priority number (low preference) so existing mail flow is unaffected.
Planned maintenance and change announcements live in Message center, not Service health.
Group-based licensing ignores nested groups - only direct members of the licensed group get licences.
Shared mailboxes do not need a licence in normal use; assign one only if you need extra storage, archive or holds.
You can never remove the initial onmicrosoft.com domain.
Microsoft 365 Backup is pay-as-you-go and requires an Azure subscription; it is not included in E3/E5 licences.
commonPitfalls: Switching MX to Microsoft 365 before mailboxes are migrated, causing mail to land in empty cloud mailboxes.
Publishing a second SPF record instead of merging includes into one TXT record (receivers treat two SPF records as an error).
Assigning licences directly AND by group, then wondering why removing the user from the group does not free the licence.
Forgetting usage location on cloud-created users in multi-country tenants, causing licence assignment errors.
Leaving Service health notifications going only to the original Global Administrator who has since left the customer.
fieldExperience: Belgian registrars frequently cap TTL or strip underscores; verify DKIM and DMARC records with an external DNS lookup, not just the admin center.
Build a PowerShell onboarding script with Microsoft Graph PowerShell (New-MgUser + group membership) and let group-based licensing do the rest - it removes 80% of licence tickets.
Put one key user per customer on Targeted release so feature changes surface a week early in your own helpdesk, not with the CEO.
revisionNotes: Verification: TXT (MS=ms...), MX with high priority value, or text file.
Service health = incidents/advisories; Message center = planned changes.
Network connectivity: configure office locations; Service Support Administrator configures, Report Reader views.
Group-based licensing: security, mail-enabled or Microsoft 365 groups; no nested groups.
Update channel for self-installs: Org settings > Services > Microsoft 365 installation options.
Microsoft 365 Backup: Exchange, OneDrive, SharePoint; pay-as-you-go via Azure subscription.

modules.title: Roles, role groups, administrative units and Privileged Identity Management
learningObjectives: Choose least-privilege Microsoft Entra and Microsoft 365 roles for common admin tasks.
Manage permissions in Defender XDR (unified RBAC) and Purview (role groups).
Delegate scoped administration with administrative units.
Configure PIM role settings, eligible assignments, approval and activation.
modules.executiveSummary:
Microsoft 365 permissions come from three layers: **Microsoft Entra built-in roles** (tenant-wide or scoped), **workload role groups** (Exchange, Purview) and **Defender XDR unified RBAC** custom roles. MS-102 expects you to pick the *least privileged* option for a task, scope it with **administrative units** where possible, and remove standing privilege with **Privileged Identity Management (PIM)**.

Microsoft recommends **fewer than five Global Administrators** and **two cloud-only emergency access (break-glass) accounts**. PIM (Entra ID P2 or Entra ID Governance) turns permanent assignments into *eligible* ones that are activated just in time with MFA, justification and optional approval.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Assigning the narrowest role that completes a task (e.g. Password Administrator or Helpdesk Administrator instead of Global Administrator).
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Limits the blast radius when an admin account is compromised.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: A container of users, groups or devices used to scope Entra role assignments.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Enables regional or departmental delegation without tenant-wide rights; AUs cannot be nested.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: A PIM assignment the user must activate before the permissions apply.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Removes standing access; activation can require MFA, justification, ticket number and approval.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Per-role configuration: max activation duration (1-24 h), MFA/authentication context, justification, approval, assignment expiry and notifications.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Allows stricter controls for high-impact roles like Global Administrator.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Custom roles in security.microsoft.com (System > Permissions) covering Defender workloads once activated.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Gives granular security-operations permissions without Entra directory roles.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Cloud-only, permanently assigned Global Administrator account excluded from blocking CA policies and protected with strong credentials (e.g. FIDO2).
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Recovers the tenant if CA, MFA or federation breaks.

modules.deepDive:
### Microsoft Entra and Microsoft 365 roles
- Roles can be assigned in admin.microsoft.com (*Roles > Role assignments* or the user's *Manage roles*) or in entra.microsoft.com (*Roles & admins*). The Microsoft 365 admin center shows a subset of Entra and Intune roles.
- Frequently tested roles: **Global Administrator**, **Global Reader**, **User Administrator**, **Helpdesk Administrator** (resets non-admin passwords), **Password Administrator**, **License Administrator**, **Groups Administrator**, **Exchange/SharePoint/Teams Administrator**, **Security Administrator/Operator/Reader**, **Compliance Administrator**, **Conditional Access Administrator**, **Authentication (Policy) Administrator**, **Privileged Role Administrator**, **Privileged Authentication Administrator**, **Hybrid Identity Administrator**, **Service Support Administrator**, **Reports Reader**.
- A Global Administrator cannot remove their own Global Administrator role. A locked-out Global Administrator can be reset by another Global Administrator or a Privileged Authentication Administrator.

### Workload permissions
- **Exchange Online**: role groups (Organization Management, Recipient Management, etc.).
- **Microsoft Purview**: role groups such as Compliance Administrator, Information Protection, eDiscovery Manager, Content Explorer List/Content viewer; many support **administrative units** so a restricted admin only sees policies for their AU.
- **Defender XDR unified RBAC**: create custom roles (permission groups *Security operations*, *Security posture*, *Authorization and settings*, *Data operations*) and **activate workloads** (Endpoint, Identity, Office 365, Cloud Apps, Exchange Online permissions). Until a workload is activated, its legacy RBAC model still applies. At least Security Administrator is needed to activate.

### Administrative units
- Create in **Entra admin center > Identity > Roles & admins > Admin units** (Privileged Role Administrator). Requires Entra ID P1 for each AU *administrator*; members only need Free.
- Adding a **group** to an AU scopes the group object, **not** its members - add users directly (or with dynamic AU rules) to manage their properties and passwords.
- **Restricted management AUs** protect objects even from tenant-level admins unless they are assigned at AU scope.

### Privileged Identity Management
- Path: **entra.microsoft.com > ID Governance > Privileged Identity Management > Microsoft Entra roles**.
- Settings per role: activation max duration 1-24 hours; require MFA or a **Conditional Access authentication context**; justification; ticket info; **approval** (select at least one approver, Microsoft recommends two); eligible/active assignment expiry; notifications.
- Approvers have **24 hours** (not configurable) to approve; approvers cannot approve their own requests.
- Lockout warning: if all Global/Privileged Role Administrators are eligible only, approval is required and no approvers are configured, you can lock yourself out - keep break-glass accounts permanently active.
- PIM for Groups provides just-in-time membership/ownership of role-assignable groups.
- Licensing: Entra ID P2 or Entra ID Governance for eligible users, approvers and reviewers. If the licence expires, eligible assignments are removed and time-bound active assignments become permanent.
modules.architecture:
### Permission evaluation
1. A user signs in and receives a token containing their **active** directory role assignments (`wids` claim) - eligible PIM roles are not present until activated.
2. Workloads evaluate: Entra roles (tenant or AU scope) -> workload role groups (Exchange/Purview) -> Defender unified RBAC (if activated).
3. **AU-scoped** roles only apply to objects that are direct members of the AU.

### PIM activation flow
`User requests activation -> PIM checks role settings -> MFA / auth context challenge -> (optional) approval request to approvers (24 h window) -> time-bound active assignment created -> audit log + notification -> assignment expires automatically`.

### Tiering for an MSP
- Tier 0: break-glass accounts (2, cloud-only, permanent GA, FIDO2, monitored sign-ins).
- Tier 1: named MSP engineers with **eligible** GA/Privileged Role Admin, approval by MSP lead.
- Tier 2: helpdesk with eligible Helpdesk Administrator scoped to customer AUs where relevant.
modules.realWorldExample:
**Scenario - 60-user engineering firm, MSP-managed**

The customer had seven permanent Global Administrators, including the CFO and a former contractor. You:
1. Create two **break-glass** accounts (`bg01@ingbureau.onmicrosoft.com`, `bg02@...`) with FIDO2 keys stored in the MSP safe and the customer's safe; exclude them from blocking CA policies and alert on any sign-in.
2. Add Entra ID P2 for the four MSP engineers and the customer IT coordinator (Business Premium only includes P1) and convert their assignments to **eligible** in PIM.
3. Set Global Administrator role settings: 2-hour max activation, MFA, justification + ticket number, approval by the MSP team lead.
4. Give the office manager **Password Administrator** scoped to an **administrative unit** containing only the Antwerp site users so she can reset passwords locally.
5. Grant the external SOC partner a Defender **unified RBAC** custom role with *Security operations* permissions only, after activating the Defender for Office 365 and Endpoint workloads.
examTips: When a question asks for the least privileged role to reset passwords for non-admins, think Helpdesk Administrator or Password Administrator, not User Administrator or Global Administrator.
PIM needs Microsoft Entra ID P2 (E5) or Entra ID Governance; Business Premium and E3 only include P1.
Managing PIM role settings requires at least Privileged Role Administrator.
Adding a group to an administrative unit does NOT put the group's members in scope.
PIM approval requests expire after 24 hours and that window is not configurable.
Microsoft recommends fewer than five Global Administrators and two cloud-only emergency access accounts.
commonPitfalls: Making every admin eligible (including break-glass accounts) and requiring approval with no approvers - risk of tenant lockout.
Assigning Global Administrator to service accounts used by scripts instead of app registrations with least-privilege Graph permissions.
Activating Defender unified RBAC before recreating custom roles, which silently removes access that came from legacy workload roles.
Forgetting that AU administrators need Entra ID P1 licences.
fieldExperience: Use GDAP (granular delegated admin privileges) from Partner Center for MSP access and keep PIM for in-tenant accounts; never use shared admin credentials.
Send PIM activation alerts to a Teams channel for the MSP team; unexpected activations are an early compromise indicator.
Document every role assignment in the customer runbook and review quarterly with an access review.
revisionNotes: Fewer than 5 GAs; 2 cloud-only break-glass GA accounts excluded from blocking CA.
PIM path: Entra admin center > ID Governance > Privileged Identity Management.
Activation 1-24 h; approval window 24 h; approver cannot self-approve.
AUs: no nesting; P1 per AU admin; group membership not inherited into scope.
Defender unified RBAC must be activated per workload (Security Administrator).

modules.title: Identity synchronization: IdFix, Connect Sync vs Cloud Sync, PHS/PTA/federation
learningObjectives: Prepare Active Directory for synchronization with IdFix and routable UPN suffixes.
Choose between Microsoft Entra Connect Sync and Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync.
Choose password hash synchronization, pass-through authentication or federation.
Monitor with Connect Health and troubleshoot common sync errors.
modules.executiveSummary:
Most Belgian SMBs still run an on-premises Active Directory, so **hybrid identity** is core MS-102 material. You prepare AD (clean attributes with **IdFix**, add a routable UPN suffix), choose a sync engine - **Microsoft Entra Connect Sync** (full sync engine on a Windows Server) or **Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync** (lightweight provisioning agents, configuration in the cloud) - and choose a sign-in method: **password hash synchronization (PHS)**, **pass-through authentication (PTA)** or **federation (AD FS)**.

Microsoft recommends **PHS** for cloud authentication and enabling PHS even when using PTA or federation, both as a disaster-recovery fallback and because **leaked credential detection** in ID Protection depends on it.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: A tool that scans on-premises AD for duplicate or invalid values in attributes such as mail, proxyAddresses and userPrincipalName.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Prevents objects from failing or being quarantined during synchronization.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: The full synchronization engine installed on a Windows Server; one active server plus optional staging server.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Supports advanced sync rules, device sync (hybrid join), PTA/AD FS configuration and large directories.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Lightweight provisioning agents on-premises; configuration and orchestration run in Microsoft Entra.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Removes the single sync server, supports multiple active agents for high availability and disconnected forests (e.g. after an acquisition).

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Syncs a hash of the AD password hash to Entra ID; authentication happens in the cloud.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Simplest, most resilient sign-in method; survives on-premises outages.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Cloud sign-in validated against AD by on-premises PTA agents (outbound connections only).
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Enforces on-premises account states (lockout, expired, logon hours) immediately without storing hashes in the cloud.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: A Connect Sync server that imports and synchronizes but does not export.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Provides disaster recovery and safe testing of configuration changes.

modules.deepDive:
### Prepare
- Remove duplicates and invalid characters in **proxyAddresses, userPrincipalName, mail, displayName, mailNickname, sAMAccountName** - IdFix reports *Duplicate*, *Blank*, *Format* errors and can apply fixes.
- Non-routable suffixes (`.local`) must get a **routable UPN suffix** matching a verified domain (e.g. `@ingbureau.be`); otherwise users sign in as `user@tenant.onmicrosoft.com`.
- Plan OU/group filtering and the source anchor (`ms-DS-ConsistencyGuid`).

### Connect Sync vs Cloud Sync (decision guide highlights)
| Capability | Connect Sync | Cloud Sync |
|---|---|---|
| Device sync / hybrid join | Yes | No |
| Multiple active instances (HA) | No (staging only) | Yes (Microsoft recommends 3 agents) |
| Disconnected forests | No | Yes |
| Advanced sync rules | Yes | Expression builder only |
| PTA configuration | Yes | No (configured separately) |
| Scale | Very large | 150K objects per domain; groups up to 50K members |
| On-demand provisioning | No | Yes |
| PHS / password writeback | Yes | Yes |
| Group provisioning to AD | No | Yes |

Both can run against the same forest if scoping is mutually exclusive.

### Sign-in methods
- **PHS**: no extra infrastructure; disabled accounts sync with up to ~30 minutes delay; required by ID Protection leaked credentials and Entra Domain Services.
- **PTA**: agents need outbound internet only; supports immediate lockout/expiry/logon hours; PTA does **not** fail over to PHS automatically - deploy multiple agents.
- **Federation (AD FS)**: needs AD FS + WAP servers and certificates; only choice for on-premises MFA/smart-card requirements; migrate to cloud auth with **staged rollout**.
- **Seamless SSO** works with PHS and PTA for domain-joined devices on the corporate network.

### Operate and troubleshoot
- Connect Sync scheduler runs every **30 minutes**: `Get-ADSyncScheduler`, `Start-ADSyncSyncCycle -PolicyType Delta` (or `Initial` for full).
- **Prevent accidental deletes** stops exports above a threshold (default 500 deletions).
- **Connect Health** (agent on the sync server) shows alerts (e.g. PHS heartbeat skipped, export stopped due to delete threshold) and sync errors with a guided fix for duplicate attributes.
- Cloud Sync: check agent status, use **Provision on demand** for one user, review provisioning logs; PHS cycles every 2-5 minutes, object provisioning roughly every 10-20 minutes.
modules.architecture:
### Connect Sync
`AD connector space -> metaverse -> Entra connector space -> Microsoft Entra ID`. Sync rules (inbound/outbound) with precedence transform attributes. Configuration lives on the server (SQL LocalDB by default), so the server is a **Tier 0** asset. A second server in **staging mode** imports/syncs but doesn't export - switch it to active if the primary fails.

### Cloud Sync
Provisioning agents (running as a **gMSA**, e.g. `provAgentgMSA$`) on domain-joined servers keep an outbound connection to the Entra provisioning service. The service holds the configuration and orchestrates; any healthy agent can process work. Agents auto-upgrade.

### Authentication paths
- **PHS**: password hash -> per-user salt + key derivation -> stored in Entra ID; cloud validates.
- **PTA**: Entra ID encrypts the password with the agent's public key and queues it on Service Bus; an agent validates against a DC and returns success/failure.
- **Federation**: Entra redirects the browser to AD FS, which issues a SAML/WS-Fed token.
modules.realWorldExample:
**Scenario - engineering firm with a 2012R2-era AD and a recent acquisition**

The firm (60 users, domain `ib.local`) acquired a 12-person surveying office with its own AD forest and no trust.
1. Run **IdFix** on both forests: fix 14 duplicate proxyAddresses and blank displayNames on service accounts; add the UPN suffix `ingbureau.be` and update users with a script.
2. Choose **Cloud Sync**: it supports the **disconnected second forest** without a trust, and two agents per forest give HA with no SQL-based sync server to patch.
3. Enable **PHS** and password writeback; keep Seamless SSO for the domain-joined CAD workstations.
4. Hybrid join is not needed because new laptops are **Entra joined** with Intune; had the customer required hybrid join, Connect Sync would have been the answer.
5. Monitor agent health in the Entra admin center and document a quarterly *Provision on demand* test in the MSP runbook.
examTips: Disconnected forests, multiple active agents, or minimal on-prem footprint -> Cloud Sync. Device sync/hybrid join, PTA config, complex sync rules -> Connect Sync.
IdFix is the answer whenever the question mentions duplicate proxyAddresses/UPNs or invalid characters before sync.
Users signing in as @tenant.onmicrosoft.com after sync usually means the on-prem UPN suffix was non-routable or unverified.
PTA does not automatically fall back to PHS - enable PHS as a backup sign-in method and switch manually.
Leaked credentials detection requires PHS, regardless of the primary authentication method.
Start-ADSyncSyncCycle -PolicyType Delta triggers an immediate delta sync on Connect Sync.
commonPitfalls: Installing Connect Sync on a member server that isn't treated as Tier 0 (patched and restricted like a DC).
Changing OU filtering and forgetting a full import, so objects don't appear or disappear as expected.
Running two active Connect Sync servers instead of one active and one staging.
Raising the accidental-delete threshold to make an error go away without checking what was going to be deleted.
Not excluding the Directory Synchronization Accounts role from Conditional Access MFA policies.
fieldExperience: For small single-forest customers, Cloud Sync with two agents (one on a DC is supported) is now the default MSP choice - fewer servers to patch.
Always enable PHS, even for customers who insist on PTA; during a ransomware incident it is what keeps email working.
Export the Connect Sync configuration before every upgrade and keep it in the customer documentation.
revisionNotes: IdFix: duplicates/invalid values in UPN, proxyAddresses, mail etc.
Cloud Sync: agents, cloud config, HA, disconnected forests, no device sync, 150K objects/domain.
Connect Sync: 30-min scheduler, staging mode, accidental delete threshold 500.
PHS recommended; PTA = on-prem validation, outbound only; federation = AD FS + WAP.
Connect Health agent monitors sync, AD FS and AD DS.

learningObjectives: Manage authentication methods in the unified Authentication methods policy.

modules.executiveSummary:
Authentication methods are now managed centrally in the **Authentication methods policy** (Entra admin center > Entra ID > Authentication methods > Policies). Managing methods in the legacy per-user MFA and SSPR policies was deprecated on 30 September 2025, so tenants must migrate (wizard or manual) to *Migration complete*.

**Self-service password reset (SSPR)** reduces helpdesk load; for synced users it requires **password writeback** via Connect Sync or Cloud Sync. **Microsoft Entra Password Protection** blocks weak passwords using the global banned list plus a custom list (up to 1,000 terms), and can be extended to on-premises DCs with a DC agent and proxy service.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Unified policy to enable methods (Microsoft Authenticator, passkeys/FIDO2, TAP, SMS, voice, OATH, email OTP, certificate-based auth) per users/groups.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Replaces separate legacy MFA and SSPR method settings and allows group targeting.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: A time-limited passcode that lets a user sign in and register strong methods.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Enables passwordless onboarding and recovery without SMS.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Writes cloud password changes/resets back to on-premises AD.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Lets hybrid users use SSPR while AD stays the source of truth.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Microsoft-maintained list of weak passwords and variants, always applied.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Blocks password-spray-friendly passwords.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Up to 1,000 organisation-specific terms (4-16 characters, case-insensitive, with substitution handling).
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Blocks company names, products and local terms.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Cloud lockout after repeated failures (default 10 attempts, 1-minute lockout, increasing).
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Slows brute force while keeping legitimate users working.

modules.deepDive:
### Authentication methods
- Migration states: **Pre-migration** (policy used for authentication only, legacy respected), **Migration in progress** (policy used for auth and SSPR, legacy still respected), **Migration complete** (only the new policy).
- Microsoft Authenticator push uses **number matching** by default. Security defaults users register Authenticator notifications.
- Prefer phishing-resistant methods (passkeys/FIDO2, Windows Hello for Business, certificate-based auth) for admins; enforce with **authentication strengths** in Conditional Access.
- Security questions remain only in the legacy SSPR settings.

### SSPR
- Enable for *None / Selected / All*; set number of methods required (1 or 2), registration requirement and re-confirmation (Microsoft suggests 90-180 days), notifications for users and admins, and a custom helpdesk link.
- Administrators always have SSPR enabled with a stronger two-method policy and cannot use security questions.
- **Writeback**: Connect Sync wizard *Optional features > Password writeback*, or Cloud Sync writeback setting; then **Entra ID > Password reset > On-premises integration > Write back passwords to your on-premises directory**. Recommended: allow users to unlock accounts without resetting.
- On-prem prerequisites: sync account needs Reset password, Write lockoutTime/pwdLastSet, Unexpire password permissions; GPO **Minimum password age = 0** if users must reset more than once per day.
- Licensing: SSPR for cloud users is in Microsoft 365 business/enterprise plans; SSPR with **on-premises writeback requires Entra ID P1** (included in Business Premium/E3).

### Password Protection
- Cloud: **Entra ID > Authentication methods > Password protection**: Enforce custom list, Custom banned password list, lockout threshold/duration.
- On-premises: install the **proxy service** (registered to Entra) and **DC agent** on every DC, set **Enable password protection on Windows Server Active Directory = Yes**, start in **Audit** mode then **Enforced**. DCs never need direct internet access; policy is enforced only where the DC agent is installed. Event IDs 10014/10017/30005 etc. in the DC Agent Admin log show results.

### Troubleshooting sign-ins
- **Sign-in logs** (status, failure reason, CA tab, authentication details), **sign-in diagnostic**, **What If** tool for CA, and the user's registered methods blade.
- Typical issues: user not registered for MFA when a policy demands it, legacy auth blocked, PTA agents down, account locked by smart lockout, CA requiring a compliant device.
modules.architecture:
### SSPR with writeback
`User at aka.ms/sspr -> verifies methods -> new password evaluated against Entra Password Protection -> sent over the Service Bus relay to Connect Sync / Cloud Sync agent -> written to AD by the sync account -> AD password policy evaluated -> success returned to user`. If AD rejects (history/complexity/min age), the user sees the error immediately.

### On-premises Password Protection
`Proxy service (outbound HTTPS to Entra) downloads policy -> stored in SYSVOL -> DC agent password filter DLL validates every change/reset on that DC -> results in event log`. No schema changes, no new DC ports, no cleartext passwords leave the DC.
modules.realWorldExample:
**Scenario - helpdesk reduction for the engineering firm**

Password reset tickets were 25% of the customer's monthly helpdesk volume.
1. Run the **authentication methods migration** wizard; enable Microsoft Authenticator and passkeys for all, SMS only for a group of 6 site engineers without smartphones.
2. Enable **SSPR** for all users, 2 methods required, with **password writeback through Cloud Sync** and *unlock without reset* enabled; set the helpdesk link to the MSP portal.
3. Add custom banned terms: `ingbureau`, `gent`, `beton`, `stabiliteit`, project codenames.
4. Install the **Password Protection proxy** on two servers and the **DC agent** on both DCs, run in **Audit** mode for three weeks, review events, then switch to **Enforced**.
5. Result after two months: password tickets down ~80%, and the next pentest found no `Company2024!`-style passwords.
examTips: SSPR for synced users needs password writeback (Connect Sync or Cloud Sync) and Entra ID P1.
On-prem Password Protection: proxy + DC agent; enforcement happens only on DCs with the agent; start in Audit mode.
Custom banned list: max 1,000 terms, 4-16 characters, case-insensitive.
Authentication methods for MFA and SSPR are managed in the Authentication methods policy; legacy method management is deprecated.
Use Temporary Access Pass to bootstrap passwordless registration.
commonPitfalls: Minimum password age GPO of 1 day causing writeback failures for users resetting twice in a day.
Disabling all methods in the policy while security defaults is on, potentially locking users out.
Expecting SMS to satisfy a phishing-resistant authentication strength.
Installing the DC agent on only one DC and assuming the whole domain is protected.
fieldExperience: Pre-register users' methods during onboarding with TAP so SSPR works from day one.
Publish the SSPR link on the Windows sign-in screen via Intune so remote users can reset without VPN.
Audit mode events are gold for a customer security report - show how many weak passwords would have been blocked.
revisionNotes: Authentication methods policy: Pre-migration -> In progress -> Complete.
SSPR writeback: Entra ID > Password reset > On-premises integration.
Password Protection: global list always; custom list optional; on-prem agent + proxy; Audit then Enforced.
Smart lockout default: 10 failures, 1-minute lockout.

modules.title: Security defaults, Conditional Access, MFA and Microsoft Entra ID Protection
learningObjectives: Decide between security defaults and Conditional Access based on licensing and requirements.
Design and roll out a Conditional Access baseline with report-only mode and exclusions.
Enforce MFA and authentication strengths through Conditional Access.
Implement user-risk and sign-in-risk policies with ID Protection.
modules.executiveSummary:
**Security defaults** give every tenant baseline protection for free: all users register for MFA, admins do MFA on every sign-in, MFA when necessary for users, legacy authentication blocked, and protection for Azure management - but no exceptions or granularity. **Conditional Access (CA)** (Entra ID P1, included in Business Premium and E3) replaces security defaults with *if-then* policies based on users, apps, conditions (location, device platform, client apps, risk) and grant/session controls. You must **disable security defaults** to use CA.

**Microsoft Entra ID Protection** (Entra ID P2 / E5) calculates **sign-in risk** and **user risk** and feeds them into CA so users can self-remediate with MFA or a secure password change.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Tenant-wide preconfigured protections enabled in Entra ID > Overview > Properties > Manage security defaults.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Gives free baseline security; not compatible with Conditional Access policies.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Assignments (users, target resources, conditions) + access controls (grant, session) + state (On, Off, Report-only).
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Applies Zero Trust decisions after first-factor authentication.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Policy evaluated and logged but not enforced.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Measures impact before enforcement; report-only policies don't need break-glass exclusions.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: A grant control that requires specific method combinations (e.g. phishing-resistant MFA).
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Lets you demand FIDO2/WHfB for admins rather than any MFA.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Probability that a specific authentication wasn't performed by the identity owner.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Usually remediated with MFA.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Probability that the account is compromised (e.g. leaked credentials).
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Usually remediated with a secure password change (or the newer risk remediation flow).

modules.deepDive:
### Security defaults vs CA
- Security defaults require registration for Microsoft Authenticator notifications (or OATH TOTP), block legacy auth (including Exchange ActiveSync basic auth), protect Azure portal/CLI/PowerShell and block device code flow for new tenants. Directory Synchronization Accounts are excluded.
- Use CA when you need exclusions, location/device conditions, compliant devices, or risk policies. Licences: P1 for CA, P2 for risk conditions.

### Baseline CA design (phase it, all start in Report-only)
1. **Block legacy authentication** (client apps: Exchange ActiveSync + other clients).
2. **Require MFA for admins** (directory roles) - ideally *phishing-resistant* authentication strength.
3. **Require MFA for all users / all resources**.
4. **Secure security info registration** (user action *Register security information* from trusted locations or with TAP).
5. **Require compliant or hybrid-joined device** (needs Intune compliance policies first).
6. **Block access from unsupported countries** (named locations).
7. Guest MFA, sign-in frequency for unmanaged devices (session controls), device code flow block.
- **Exclusions**: emergency access accounts (group), Directory Synchronization Accounts role, service accounts (prefer workload identities).
- Tools: **What If**, **policy impact**, **Conditional Access insights and reporting workbook**, sign-in logs CA tab.
- Templates: many policies are available as **Conditional Access templates** that default to report-only. **Microsoft-managed policies** may be created automatically in report-only mode.

### Grant control logic
- *Require all the selected controls* (AND) vs *Require one of the selected controls* (OR). Block overrides everything; multiple policies are all evaluated and every applicable policy must be satisfied.

### ID Protection
- Detections include anonymous IP, atypical travel, leaked credentials (needs PHS), malware-linked IP, password spray, suspicious inbox rules (from Defender for Cloud Apps/Office 365).
- Configure **risk-based CA policies** (do not combine user risk and sign-in risk in one policy): sign-in risk Medium+High -> require MFA; user risk High -> require secure password change (or *require risk remediation*) + sign-in frequency every time.
- Users must be MFA-registered before risk occurs; risky users can't register MFA during a risky session (AADSTS53004).
- Reports: Risky users, Risky sign-ins, Risk detections (full detail with P2).
modules.architecture:
### Evaluation pipeline
`First-factor authentication -> Entra collects signals (user, groups/roles, app, IP/named location, device state from Intune/hybrid join, client app, risk from ID Protection) -> all enabled policies whose assignments match are evaluated -> grant controls combined (block wins) -> session controls applied -> token issued`. Report-only policies are evaluated and written to the sign-in log without affecting the outcome.

### Risk pipeline
`Real-time and offline detections (Microsoft threat intelligence, Defender signals) -> risk level per sign-in and per user -> CA policy with risk condition -> user self-remediates (MFA / password change) -> risk dismissed automatically`.
modules.realWorldExample:
**Scenario - moving the engineering firm from security defaults to CA**

The firm has Business Premium (P1), so risk-based policies are not available unless the MSP adds Entra ID P2 for selected users.
1. Create a group `CA-Exclude-BreakGlass` with the two emergency accounts.
2. Build six policies from templates in **Report-only**: block legacy auth, MFA for admins (phishing-resistant strength), MFA for all users, compliant device for Windows/macOS, block outside EU + UK, secure MFA registration.
3. Review two weeks of sign-in logs and the CA workbook: an old multifunction printer uses SMTP AUTH - move it to SMTP relay via connector.
4. **Disable security defaults** and switch the policies to **On** in one maintenance window, admin policies first.
5. Add Entra ID P2 for the directors and finance (high-value targets) and enable a sign-in-risk policy scoped to that group.
6. Quarterly test of the break-glass accounts is added to the MSP checklist.
examTips: Security defaults and Conditional Access are mutually exclusive - disable security defaults before enabling CA policies.
CA requires Entra ID P1 (Business Premium, E3); risk-based conditions require Entra ID P2 (E5).
Always exclude emergency access accounts from blocking CA policies; report-only policies don't need the exclusion.
Don't combine user risk and sign-in risk in the same policy.
Leaked credentials detection needs password hash synchronization for hybrid users.
Use the What If tool to explain why a policy did or didn't apply to a sign-in.
commonPitfalls: Enabling 'require compliant device' for all users before any Intune compliance policy exists.
Targeting 'All users' with a block policy and forgetting the sync account and break-glass exclusions.
Assuming per-user MFA 'Enforced' status is needed - with CA, users show Disabled in the legacy per-user MFA page.
Using IP-based named locations as the only control for admin access.
fieldExperience: Keep a standard MSP CA policy set with a naming convention (CA001-Block-LegacyAuth...) and deploy it the same way to every customer.
Report-only for at least one full business cycle (month-end closing!) catches finance apps that still use legacy protocols.
When a director travels outside the allowed countries, use a time-bound exclusion group rather than editing the policy.
revisionNotes: Security defaults: free, all-or-nothing; CA: P1; risk: P2.
Policy states: Off, Report-only, On.
Grant: block, require MFA, authentication strength, compliant device, hybrid joined, approved app/app protection, password change.
Sign-in risk -> MFA; user risk -> secure password change.
Exclude break-glass and Directory Synchronization Accounts role.

learningObjectives: Use Microsoft Secure Score and Exposure Management recommendations to prioritise hardening.
Triage incidents and alerts and use advanced hunting (KQL) in the Defender portal.
Use Defender XDR reports, alert policies and threat intelligence (threat analytics / Defender TI).
Understand licensing across Defender XDR components for SMB customers.
modules.executiveSummary:
The **Microsoft Defender portal** (security.microsoft.com) unifies Defender for Endpoint, Defender for Office 365, Defender for Identity and Defender for Cloud Apps into **incidents** - correlated groups of alerts across identities, endpoints, email and apps. MS-102 focuses on the administrator view: improving posture with **Microsoft Secure Score** (now surfaced through **Microsoft Security Exposure Management**), reviewing incidents/alerts, running **advanced hunting** queries over 30 days of raw data, configuring **alert policies**, reading reports and consuming **threat intelligence**.

For an MSP, Secure Score is also the most understandable KPI for a customer's quarterly business review.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: A correlated collection of alerts and evidence representing one attack story.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Lets responders work one attack instead of dozens of alerts.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: A score of achieved vs possible points across identity, device, apps and data recommendations.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Measures and prioritises security posture improvements.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Unified posture area (initiatives, metrics, recommendations, attack surface) in the Defender portal.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Shows exposure across workloads and tracks security initiatives.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: KQL-based query tool over up to 30 days of raw Defender XDR data (guided or advanced mode).
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Proactive threat hunting and custom detection rules.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Rule that generates alerts (and optional email notifications) when activities match conditions.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Notifies admins of risky activity such as forwarding rules or users restricted from sending.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Microsoft research reports and intel on actors, campaigns and vulnerabilities with your exposure data.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Helps decide which emerging threats matter to your environment.

modules.deepDive:
### Secure Score
- Path: **security.microsoft.com/securescore** - Overview, **Recommended actions**, History, Metrics & trends.
- Each recommended action is worth **10 points or less**; most are binary, some partial (e.g. % of users with MFA).
- Statuses: *To address*, *Planned*, *Risk accepted* (no points), *Resolved through third party* / *alternate mitigation* (points awarded), *Completed* (verified by Microsoft data). Changes can take **24-48 hours** to reflect.
- Views: Current license score, Achievable score, Planned score. The full set of recommendations is shown regardless of licences.
- Device recommendations route to **Defender Vulnerability Management** (you can't set a status for them in Secure Score).

### Incidents and alerts
- **Incidents & alerts > Incidents**: assign, classify (true/false positive), set status, review attack story, evidence, and automated investigation results.
- **Automated investigation and response (AIR)** is available with MDO Plan 2 / MDE Plan 2 / Defender for Business; actions can need approval in the **Action center**.
- Defender data is retained **180 days** in the portal; advanced hunting queries see **30 days** unless data is streamed to Microsoft Sentinel.

### Advanced hunting
- Tables such as `DeviceProcessEvents`, `EmailEvents`, `EmailUrlInfo`, `IdentityLogonEvents`, `CloudAppEvents`, `AlertInfo`.
- Limits: 30-day range, 100,000 rows, 10-minute timeout, UTC timestamps.
- Save queries as **custom detection rules** to alert or take actions automatically.

### Reports and alert policies
- Reports: Email & collaboration reports (Threat protection status, Mailflow status, compromised users), Endpoint reports (device health, AV), Identity reports.
- **Alert policies** (Email & collaboration > Policies & rules > Alert policy): default *System* policies (e.g. *Creation of forwarding/redirect rule*, *Email sending limit exceeded*, *User restricted from sending email*) can be toggled and have recipients changed; custom policies need Manage Alerts or Organization Configuration roles and take up to 24 hours to become active. Advanced (threshold/anomaly) alerting needs E5 or add-ons.

### Threat intelligence
- **Threat intelligence > Overview / Intel explorer** (formerly Threat analytics & Defender TI) - reports with *Impacted assets*, *Exposure and mitigations* and recommended actions.
- Defender TI Premium adds Microsoft IOCs and enriched OSINT; Standard gives public IOCs and limited intel profiles.
modules.architecture:
### Signal flow
`MDE sensor (devices) + MDO (mail/Teams/SharePoint) + MDI sensor (DCs) + MDCA (cloud apps) + Entra ID Protection -> Defender XDR correlation engine -> alerts -> incidents -> AIR playbooks -> Action center`. Raw events land in advanced hunting tables; posture data feeds Secure Score / Exposure Management.

### Permissions
Defender portal access comes from Entra roles (Security Administrator, Security Operator, Security Reader, Global Reader) or Defender **unified RBAC** custom roles after workloads are activated.
modules.realWorldExample:
**Scenario - quarterly security review for the engineering firm**

Secure Score is 48%. You:
1. Filter **Recommended actions** by *Identity* and *low user impact*: enable MFA for all users (already via CA - mark completed once data syncs), block legacy auth, turn on Safe Links/Attachments presets.
2. Mark *Risk accepted* for "Require a compliant device for all users" for the 3 shared CAD render nodes - documented with a compensating control.
3. Investigate an incident *"Multi-stage incident involving initial access & persistence"*: a project manager clicked a phishing link, an inbox forwarding rule was created (default alert policy fired). Use **advanced hunting** on `EmailUrlInfo` and `CloudAppEvents` to find the two other recipients who clicked.
4. Read the **threat analytics** report on the active AiTM phishing campaign and confirm the mitigation (phishing-resistant MFA for admins) is in place.
5. Present the Secure Score trend (48% -> 71%) in the QBR deck.
examTips: Risk accepted gives no Secure Score points; resolved through third party/alternate mitigation does.
Advanced hunting covers 30 days of raw Defender XDR data; the portal retains data for 180 days.
Advanced hunting supports guided (query builder) and advanced (KQL) modes; queries can become custom detection rules.
New or changed alert policies can take up to 24 hours to start generating alerts.
Device-related Secure Score actions are managed through Defender Vulnerability Management recommendations.
commonPitfalls: Chasing Secure Score points for actions that break business processes instead of documenting risk acceptance.
Assuming every customer has AIR - Business Premium gets AIR for endpoints through Defender for Business but not MDO Plan 2 features.
Not changing default alert policy recipients from TenantAdmins to the MSP monitoring mailbox.
fieldExperience: Export Secure Score history monthly to the customer report; trend lines persuade budget holders better than raw percentages.
Keep a shared library of KQL hunting queries (forwarding rules, OAuth consent, impossible travel) and run them across customers after major campaigns.
Use Microsoft 365 Lighthouse for multi-tenant incident visibility in SMB customers.
revisionNotes: Secure Score: <=10 points per action; 24-48h update; risk accepted = 0 points.
Incidents group alerts; classify and resolve; AIR actions in Action center.
Advanced hunting: 30 days, KQL, 100k rows, 10-min timeout.
Alert policies: Email & collaboration > Policies & rules > Alert policy.
Threat intelligence: Overview + Intel explorer; Defender TI Standard vs Premium.

modules.title: Defender for Office 365: presets, Safe Links, Safe Attachments, simulations and restricted entities

Configure Safe Links and Safe Attachments (including Dynamic Delivery).

modules.executiveSummary:
Every cloud mailbox gets the built-in **Exchange Online Protection (EOP)** features: anti-malware, anti-spam, anti-spoofing. **Microsoft Defender for Office 365 (MDO)** adds **Safe Links** (URL rewriting and time-of-click checks in email, Teams and Office apps), **Safe Attachments** (detonation sandbox, also for SharePoint/OneDrive/Teams), **impersonation protection**, investigation tools and, in **Plan 2**, Threat Explorer, AIR and **Attack simulation training**.

The fastest, Microsoft-recommended configuration is the **preset security policies**: *Standard* for most users, *Strict* for high-value targets, and *Built-in protection* which by default gives Safe Links and Safe Attachments to everyone not covered by other policies.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Microsoft-managed profiles (Standard, Strict, Built-in protection) whose settings update automatically.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Delivers best-practice protection without tuning dozens of settings.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Strict > Standard > MDO evaluation > custom policies (by priority) > Built-in protection / default policies.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Determines which settings apply when a recipient is in multiple policies.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: URL scanning and rewriting during mail flow plus time-of-click verification in email, Teams and Office apps.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Protects against links that become malicious after delivery.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Sandbox detonation of attachments; Dynamic Delivery delivers the body immediately with attachment placeholders.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Catches zero-day malware without delaying business email.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Retroactively moves already-delivered malware/phish/spam messages.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Handles threats that are identified after delivery.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Users or connectors blocked from sending due to outbound spam/limit violations (NDR 5.1.8 for users).
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Contains compromised accounts that are spamming.

modules.deepDive:
### Licensing
- **EOP**: all cloud mailboxes. **MDO Plan 1**: Business Premium, or add-on (Safe Links, Safe Attachments, anti-phishing impersonation, real-time detections). **MDO Plan 2**: Microsoft 365 E5 / Defender Suite (Threat Explorer, AIR, Attack simulation training, campaign views, threat trackers).

### Preset policies
- Path: **security.microsoft.com > Email & collaboration > Policies & rules > Threat policies > Preset security policies** (Templated policies).
- Standard/Strict are assigned to **no one** until you turn them on and choose recipients (users, groups, domains) separately for EOP protections and MDO protections, and add **impersonation protection** entries.
- Built-in protection applies to all recipients by default; you can only configure **exceptions**.
- Differences: Built-in allows click-through and doesn't apply Safe Links to internal senders; Standard/Strict don't allow click-through and do scan internal mail.
- Policies use special rules: `Get-EOPProtectionPolicyRule`, `Get-ATPProtectionPolicyRule`, `Get-ATPBuiltInProtectionRule`.

### Safe Links
- Options: on for email (URLs rewritten by default), apply to internal email, real-time scanning of suspicious links and links to files, wait for scan to complete before delivery, *Do not rewrite URLs - API checks only*, Teams, Office apps, click-through, *Do not rewrite the following URLs* list.
- A universal allow for URLs belongs in the **Tenant Allow/Block List** (via submissions), not only in the per-policy do-not-rewrite list.

### Safe Attachments
- Unknown malware response: Off, **Monitor**, **Block**, **Dynamic Delivery**. Redirect is available with Monitor. Quarantine policy defaults to AdminOnlyAccessPolicy - users can only *request* release of malware/phish.
- Dynamic Delivery can't replace attachments for public folders, S/MIME, on-premises recipients or mail routed out and back in (e.g. some signature services).
- **Safe Attachments for SharePoint, OneDrive and Teams** is a global setting (in MDO P1+), with an optional alert policy for detected files.

### Investigation and response
- Real-time detections (P1) / **Threat Explorer** (P2), email entity page, **Submissions** (report false positives/negatives), **quarantine**, ZAP, message trace.
- **Alert policies** for MDO (e.g. *Email reported by user as malware or phish*, *Malware not zapped because ZAP is disabled*).

### Attack simulation training
- **Email & collaboration > Attack simulation training** (https://security.microsoft.com/attacksimulator). Requires **E5 or MDO Plan 2** for the targeted users (a limited trial exists for E3).
- Techniques: credential harvest, malware attachment, link in attachment, link to malware, drive-by URL, OAuth consent grant, how-to guide; payloads (global, tenant, MDO recommendations); assign training; **training campaigns** without a simulation; simulation automations.
- Roles: Attack Simulation Administrator, Attack Payload Author, Security Administrator.

### Restricted entities
- When a user exceeds outbound limits or outbound spam policy limits, they're blocked from sending (NDR **550 5.1.8 Access denied, bad outbound sender**), added to **Email & collaboration > Review > Restricted entities**, and the default alert **User restricted from sending email** fires.
- Before unblocking: reset password, revoke sessions, enable MFA, remove malicious inbox/forwarding rules. Unblock in the portal or `Remove-BlockedSenderAddress`; removal usually within 1 hour (max 24 h).
- Outbound spam policy action can be *restrict until the following day* (default) or *restrict until admin removes*.
modules.architecture:
### Mail filtering stack
1. **Edge protection** - connection filtering, IP reputation, throttling.
2. **Sender intelligence** - SPF, DKIM, DMARC, spoof intelligence, impersonation (MDO).
3. **Content filtering** - anti-malware, anti-spam, Safe Attachments detonation, URL detonation.
4. **Post-delivery** - Safe Links time-of-click, ZAP, user reporting, AIR, Safe Attachments for SPO/ODB/Teams.

Policies are evaluated per recipient following precedence; once a recipient matches a policy of a type, lower-priority policies of that type are ignored.
modules.realWorldExample:
**Scenario - invoice-fraud wave hitting Belgian construction firms**

The finance team of the engineering firm receives convincing fake supplier invoices.
1. Turn on **Standard preset** for all users and **Strict preset** for finance + directors; add the CEO and CFO and the two biggest suppliers' domains to **impersonation protection**.
2. Keep Built-in protection for everyone else (shared mailboxes) and confirm via `Get-ATPBuiltInProtectionRule`.
3. A user clicks a link anyway: Safe Links blocks at time of click; Threat Explorer isn't available (Business Premium = MDO P1), so use **real-time detections** to find other recipients and soft-delete the messages.
4. A month later a mailbox is compromised and starts spamming: the user appears in **Restricted entities**; you reset the password, revoke sessions, remove a hidden inbox rule, then unblock.
5. Upsell the Defender Suite add-on to get **Attack simulation training** for quarterly phishing campaigns.
examTips: Standard and Strict presets apply to nobody until you assign recipients; Built-in protection applies to everyone by default.
Precedence: Strict, then Standard, then evaluation policies, then custom policies, then Built-in protection/default policies.
Dynamic Delivery = deliver the body now, attachment placeholder until scanning finishes.
Attack simulation training requires Microsoft 365 E5 or Defender for Office 365 Plan 2.
Users blocked for outbound spam get NDR 5.1.8 and appear on the Restricted entities page.
Business Premium includes Defender for Office 365 Plan 1, not Plan 2.
commonPitfalls: Creating custom policies that conflict with presets and expecting the custom settings to win.
Unblocking a restricted user before securing the account - they get restricted again within the hour.
Using Dynamic Delivery with third-party signature services that route mail out and back in without the bypass header.
Allow-listing domains in anti-spam policies, which bypasses filtering for spoofed senders.
fieldExperience: Presets are the MSP default: they update automatically and are easy to explain in an audit.
Belgian customers often use Exclaimer/CodeTwo signatures - test Safe Attachments Dynamic Delivery before rollout.
Run Attack simulation training quarterly with localized (Dutch/French) payloads; report click-rates per department to management.
revisionNotes: Presets path: Email & collaboration > Policies & rules > Threat policies > Preset security policies.
Safe Links: time-of-click, URL rewrite, Teams, Office apps.
Safe Attachments actions: Off, Monitor, Block, Dynamic Delivery.
Restricted entities: Email & collaboration > Review > Restricted entities; Remove-BlockedSenderAddress.
AST: E5 / MDO P2; Attack Simulation Administrator role.

modules.title: Defender for Endpoint, Vulnerability Management and Defender for Cloud Apps
learningObjectives: Onboard devices to Defender for Endpoint via Intune and configure endpoint settings.
Act on Defender Vulnerability Management dashboards and recommendations.
Connect Microsoft 365 to Defender for Cloud Apps and create policies.
Configure Cloud App Discovery (including MDE integration) and sanction/unsanction apps.
modules.executiveSummary:
**Microsoft Defender for Endpoint (MDE)** provides next-generation protection, attack surface reduction, EDR and automated investigation for devices. In Business Premium the equivalent is **Defender for Business** (MDE Plan 1 plus selected Plan 2 features, up to 300 users). Onboarding is easiest through the **Intune connection**: Intune receives the onboarding package automatically and an **EDR policy** deploys it.

**Defender Vulnerability Management (MDVM)** turns sensor data into an **exposure score**, **Secure Score for Devices** and prioritised **security recommendations** with Intune remediation tickets.

**Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps (MDCA)** is Microsoft's CASB: **app connectors** (e.g. Microsoft 365) give API-level visibility, **policies** raise alerts and governance actions, and **Cloud App Discovery** finds shadow IT from firewall logs or, simplest, from **MDE network data**, with the option to block unsanctioned apps on endpoints.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Configuration that connects a device's sensor to your MDE tenant; deployed via Intune EDR policy ('Auto from connector'), GPO, script, ConfigMgr.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Without onboarding, the device sends no telemetry and gets no EDR.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Rules that block risky behaviours (e.g. Office spawning child processes).
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Reduce exploit opportunities; deploy in audit first.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: MDVM score of device exposure to threats; lower is better.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Prioritises vulnerability remediation.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: API connection from MDCA to a cloud app such as Microsoft 365.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Provides activity logs, files and governance actions for that app.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Analysis of traffic logs against a catalog of 31,000+ cloud apps scored on 90+ risk factors.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Reveals shadow IT and its risk.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: App tagged as prohibited in MDCA, synchronized to MDE as a network indicator.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Allows blocking risky cloud apps on endpoints anywhere, without a proxy.

modules.deepDive:
### Defender for Endpoint onboarding
1. Defender portal: **System > Settings > Endpoints > General > Advanced features > Intune connection = On**.
2. Intune admin center: **Endpoint security > Microsoft Defender for Endpoint** shows connection *Enabled*.
3. Create **Endpoint security > Endpoint detection and response** policy (Windows) with *Microsoft Defender for Endpoint client configuration package type = Auto from connector* - or use *Deploy preconfigured policy* to target all devices.
4. Configure **Antivirus**, **ASR rules** (audit first), **network protection** and firewall via endpoint security policies; or use security settings management for non-Intune devices.
5. Validate with the **detection test** command and the device inventory; Intune's EDR Onboarding Status tab shows progress.
- Required roles: **Endpoint Security Manager** (Intune) and **Security Administrator** (Entra) for the connection.
- Other methods: local script (up to small numbers of devices), Group Policy, Configuration Manager, VDI scripts, Defender deployment tool. Servers need Defender for Servers / Defender for Business servers licences.
- Onboarding a device to MDE also onboards it to **Endpoint DLP**.

### Defender Vulnerability Management
- **Exposure management > Vulnerability management > Overview / Dashboard**: exposure score, Secure Score for Devices, top recommendations, vulnerable software, remediation activities, exposed devices, event timeline, expiring certificates.
- Select a recommendation > **Request remediation** (due date, notes) -> creates a remediation activity and an **Intune security task**; or create an **exception** (global or per device group).
- Devices inactive for 30+ days are excluded from scores.

### Defender for Cloud Apps
- **Connect Microsoft 365**: Defender portal **Settings > Cloud Apps > Connected apps > App Connectors > + Connect an app > Microsoft 365**, select all components; enable file monitoring for files.
- **Policies** (Cloud Apps > Policies > Policy management): activity policies (single or repeated activity, e.g. mass download), anomaly detection policies (impossible travel, activity from infrequent country, ransomware, mass deletion - built in and machine-learned), app discovery policies, OAuth app policies; **governance actions** such as suspend user, require sign-in again, notify user. File policies are being retired (6 January 2027) in favour of Purview DLP/auto-labeling.
- **Activity log**: filter by app, user, IP, activity type; drill into user insights.
- **Cloud Discovery**: snapshot reports (manual upload), continuous reports via **log collector**, or native **MDE integration** (Settings > Endpoints > Advanced features > Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps = On; data visible within about 2 hours). Mark apps **Sanctioned / Unsanctioned / Monitored**; unsanctioned apps are blocked on MDE devices via network protection within about 3 hours.
- **Office 365 Cloud App Security** is a limited edition (750+ apps, manual log upload only).
modules.architecture:
### Endpoint
`Windows sensor (built into Windows) + Defender Antivirus -> MDE cloud -> alerts/incidents in Defender XDR -> Intune receives device risk for compliance -> Conditional Access can require 'device at or under risk level'`.

### Cloud apps
`Microsoft 365 audit/API data -> MDCA app connector -> activity log, anomaly engine -> alerts in Defender XDR`. Discovery: `MDE network events -> MDCA discovery -> app risk catalog -> unsanctioned tag -> MDE custom network indicators -> network protection blocks domains on device`.
modules.realWorldExample:
**Scenario - shadow IT and endpoint hardening at the engineering firm**

1. Connect Intune and MDE, deploy the **preconfigured EDR policy** to all Windows devices, then an ASR policy in **audit** mode. After 2 weeks, switch most ASR rules to block; keep "Block Office apps from creating child processes" in audit for a legacy macro-based calculation tool.
2. MDVM shows an outdated AutoCAD plug-in and 7-Zip with critical CVEs: **Request remediation** creates Intune tasks; packaging updates via Intune Win32 apps closes them in a week; exposure score drops from 62 to 31.
3. Turn on the **MDCA integration** in MDE Advanced features. Cloud Discovery reveals WeTransfer, two free PDF converters and a Chinese file-sharing app used for drawings. Mark the file-sharing app **Unsanctioned** - blocked on all laptops, including at construction sites outside the office network.
4. Connect the **Microsoft 365 app connector** and create an activity policy for mass downloads from the Projects SharePoint site, with *notify user* and an alert to the MSP.
examTips: Fastest MDE onboarding for Intune-managed Windows: enable the Intune connection, then an EDR policy using 'Auto from connector'.
Business Premium includes Defender for Business (MDE P1 + some P2 features), not full MDE Plan 2.
Lower exposure score is better; higher Secure Score for Devices is better.
Cloud Discovery from endpoints without proxies or log collectors = turn on the MDCA integration in MDE Advanced features.
Unsanctioned apps are blocked on devices through MDE network protection.
Microsoft 365 app connector: Settings > Cloud Apps > Connected apps > App Connectors.
commonPitfalls: Enabling all ASR rules in block mode on day one and breaking line-of-business macros.
Forgetting that network protection must be enabled (block mode) for unsanctioned-app blocking to work.
Expecting Cloud Discovery data from the MDE integration for macOS/Linux devices without checking supported platforms.
Onboarding servers with workstation licences.
fieldExperience: In Business Premium tenants, the simplified Defender for Business setup wizard is fine for small customers; use Intune endpoint security policies for MSP standardisation.
Report the exposure score trend next to Secure Score in QBRs; customers understand 'fewer vulnerable devices'.
Tag CAD and engineering apps as Sanctioned early to avoid false shadow-IT alarms.
revisionNotes: MDE + Intune: Advanced features > Intune connection; EDR policy 'Auto from connector'.
Roles: Endpoint Security Manager (Intune) + Security Administrator (Entra).
MDVM: exposure score, Secure Score for Devices, Request remediation -> Intune task.
MDCA: app connectors, activity/anomaly/discovery policies, governance actions, activity log.
Discovery sources: snapshot upload, log collector, MDE integration.
