modules.title: Purview information protection and data lifecycle: SITs, sensitivity labels, retention
learningObjectives: Create custom sensitive information types with regex, keyword lists and dictionaries.
Create, configure and publish sensitivity labels and label policies.
Implement retention policies, retention labels and label policies and apply the principles of retention.
Monitor labeling with Content explorer, Activity explorer and reports.
modules.executiveSummary:
Microsoft Purview protects and governs data in Microsoft 365. **Sensitive information types (SITs)** detect patterns such as IBANs or Belgian national register numbers; custom SITs use **regular expressions, keyword lists, keyword dictionaries or functions**, with supporting elements, proximity and confidence levels.

**Sensitivity labels** classify and protect content (encryption, content marking, container settings for Teams/Groups/Sites) and are made available through **label policies**. **Retention** keeps or deletes content: **retention policies** apply to containers (mailboxes, sites, Teams), **retention labels** apply to individual items. When settings conflict, the **principles of retention** decide.

Monitoring uses **Content explorer** (what sensitive/labeled content exists where) and **Activity explorer** (what users did with it).

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Pattern definition: primary element (regex, keyword list, dictionary, function) + supporting elements + proximity + confidence level.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Lets DLP, auto-labeling and retention detect sensitive content.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Classification with optional encryption, markings, auto-labeling and container settings.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Protection travels with the document or email wherever it goes.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Publishes labels to users/groups with settings such as default label, mandatory labeling and justification for downgrade.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Labels are invisible to users until published.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Container-level retain/delete settings (Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams, Viva Engage, Copilot).
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Broad compliance retention with low administrative overhead.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Item-level retain/delete settings applied manually or automatically; one per item.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Exceptions (e.g. contracts kept 10 years) and records management.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Purview data classification tools for content at rest and user activities on labeled/sensitive content.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Measure adoption and spot risky behaviour.

modules.deepDive:
### Sensitive information types
- Path: **purview.microsoft.com > Information Protection > Classifiers > Sensitive info types > Create sensitive info type**.
- Patterns with **High/Medium/Low confidence**; primary element (regex with optional validator, keyword list, keyword dictionary, function); supporting elements; **character proximity**; additional checks.
- Regex rules: no positional anchors (`^`, `$`), a single capturing group; Boost.RegEx engine. Keyword dictionaries are case-insensitive and limited to 1 MB compressed across the tenant.
- Copy a built-in SIT to customise it; new SITs only match existing SharePoint content after re-crawl. Exact Data Match (EDM) for database-backed matching.

### Sensitivity labels
- Create labels in **Information Protection > Sensitivity labels** (scope: files & other data assets, emails, meetings, groups & sites, schematized data). Settings: encryption (assign permissions now or let users assign), content marking (header, footer, watermark), auto-labeling for files and emails (client-side), group/site settings (privacy, external sharing, guest access).
- **Label priority** order matters: higher order = more sensitive; used for downgrade justification and DLP conditions.
- Publish via **Publishing policies > Publish label**: choose labels, admin units, users/groups, then **default label** (documents, emails, meetings, Power BI), **require justification** to remove/lower a label, **mandatory labeling**, **help link**. Changes can take up to **24 hours** to replicate.
- Sublabels: don't set a parent label as default.
- Default labels (Personal, Public, General, Confidential, Highly Confidential) and a default policy can be auto-created for new customers.
- Service-side **auto-labeling policies** (SharePoint/OneDrive/Exchange) run in simulation first and require E5-class licensing; manual labeling is included in Business Premium/E3.
- Enable sensitivity labels for Office files in SharePoint/OneDrive to support co-authoring, search and eDiscovery of encrypted files.

### Retention
- **Data lifecycle management > Retention policies** (static scope or adaptive scope) and **Retention labels** + **label policies** (publish for manual application or auto-apply by SIT, keywords/KQL, trainable classifier).
- Principles of retention: 1) **retention wins over deletion**; 2) **longest retention period wins**; 3) **explicit wins over implicit for deletion** (label delete beats policy delete; scoped policy beats org-wide policy); 4) **shortest deletion period wins**.
- An item can have only **one retention label**. eDiscovery holds always preserve content. **Preservation Lock** prevents anyone (including admins) from weakening a policy.
- Retained SharePoint/OneDrive content goes to the **Preservation Hold Library**; Exchange content to **Recoverable Items**.

### Monitoring
- **Content explorer**: access to the tab via Compliance/Security Administrator or Information Protection roles; viewing item lists needs **Content Explorer List viewer**, viewing item contents needs **Content Explorer Content viewer**.
- **Activity explorer**: label applied/changed/removed, DLP rule matches, file copied to USB, etc.
- Data classification analytics (Content & Activity explorer UI) require E5/A5/G5-level licensing; Posture/label reports show a rolling 30-day window.
modules.architecture:
### Labeling pipeline
`Admin creates label (Purview) -> label policy published -> clients (Office apps built-in labeling, Purview Information Protection client, SharePoint/Exchange services) download policy -> label metadata stamped in file/email -> if encryption: Azure Rights Management issues use licences -> activity events -> Activity explorer`.

### Classification index
SharePoint/OneDrive/Exchange content is indexed and evaluated against SITs and trainable classifiers; results feed Content explorer, DLP, auto-labeling and retention auto-apply.

### Retention evaluation
For each item, all applicable retention settings are evaluated independently for *retain* and *delete* actions; the principles of retention resolve conflicts (see retention flowchart).
modules.realWorldExample:
**Scenario - protecting design drawings and HR data**

1. Create a custom SIT *Project number* with regex `IB-[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{3}` (no anchors) and keyword supporting elements `project`, `werf`, `chantier` within 300 characters; High confidence when both match.
2. Labels: *Public*, *General*, *Confidential* (footer + watermark), *Confidential - Clients* (encryption: co-owner internal, viewer for specified client domains), *Highly Confidential - HR* (encryption: HR group only).
3. Publish to all users with default label *General* for documents and emails and justification for downgrades.
4. Retention: org-wide policy **retain 7 years** for Exchange/SharePoint/OneDrive (Belgian accounting obligations - confirm with the customer's accountant); retention label *Contract - 10 years* published for manual use by project managers.
5. After a month, use **Activity explorer** to show management how often labels are downgraded and by whom.
examTips: Labels do nothing for users until they are published in a label policy.
Retention policy = containers; retention label = individual items (only one label per item).
Principles of retention: retention beats deletion, longest retention wins, explicit beats implicit for deletion, shortest deletion wins.
Content explorer item lists need Content Explorer List viewer; item contents need Content Explorer Content viewer.
Custom SIT regex must not use ^ or $ anchors and should use a single capturing group.
commonPitfalls: Setting an encryption label as the default label, breaking external sharing with clients.
Making a parent label the default when sublabels exist.
Expecting a new SIT to match existing SharePoint documents without a re-crawl.
Using eDiscovery holds for long-term retention instead of retention policies.
fieldExperience: Start with five labels maximum; SMB users ignore complex taxonomies.
Agree retention periods with the customer's accountant/legal advisor - the MSP implements, it doesn't decide legal retention.
Pilot labels with the management team for two weeks before publishing to all users.
revisionNotes: SIT parts: primary element, supporting elements, proximity, confidence.
Label policy settings: default label, mandatory labeling, justification, help link; up to 24 h to replicate.
Retention principles (4 levels).
Explorers: Content explorer (at rest), Activity explorer (actions).

modules.title: Purview DLP for Microsoft 365 workloads, Endpoint DLP and insider risk basics
learningObjectives: Create DLP policies for Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams, Power BI and Microsoft 365 Copilot.
Roll out policies safely with simulation mode, policy tips and staged actions.
Configure Endpoint DLP and onboard devices.
Review DLP alerts, Activity explorer events and reports; know the insider risk management basics.
modules.executiveSummary:
**Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP)** monitors and protects sensitive items in Microsoft 365 services and on endpoints. A DLP policy defines **what** to protect (SITs, labels, classifiers), **where** (locations), **conditions** and **actions** (audit, block with override, block) plus user notifications (**policy tips**) and alerts.

Deploy policies in stages: **Keep it off** -> **Run the policy in simulation mode** -> **simulation with policy tips** -> **Turn it on**. **Endpoint DLP** extends protection to Windows 10/11 (1809+) and macOS devices for actions like copy to USB, upload to cloud, print, and paste to browsers. **Insider risk management** correlates signals (e.g. HR resignation + mass download) into risk-scored alerts.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Where a policy applies: Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams chat/channel, Devices, on-premises repositories, Fabric/Power BI, Defender for Cloud Apps instances, Microsoft 365 Copilot.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Scopes enforcement per workload.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Policy state that evaluates and reports matches (up to 15 days per simulation) without enforcing actions.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Tune false positives before users are affected.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: In-app notification to users when content matches a DLP rule.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Educates users and supports override with justification.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Action blocking the activity but allowing the user to override with a business justification.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Balances protection and productivity and surfaces false positives.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: DLP for onboarded devices monitoring file activities (copy to USB, network share, cloud upload, print, clipboard, unallowed apps/browsers).
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Stops exfiltration paths outside cloud services.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Purview solution using policy templates (e.g. data theft by departing users) and pseudonymised alerts.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Detects risky user behaviour that single DLP events miss.

modules.deepDive:
### Building a DLP policy
- Path: **purview.microsoft.com > Solutions > Data loss prevention > Policies > Create policy** (templates by category/regulation, or custom).
- Admin units can scope a policy; choose locations and include/exclude specific sites, groups, accounts or devices.
- Rules: conditions (content contains SIT with min count and confidence, sensitivity label, shared outside the organisation, document properties), exceptions, actions (restrict access/encrypt, block, block with override, audit), **user notifications** (policy tips, email), **incident reports/alerts** (severity, thresholds).
- **Actions by stage**: *Allow* (devices only) / *Audit only* -> *Block with override* -> *Block*.
- **Policy states**: Keep it off; Run the policy in simulation mode; simulation with policy tips; Turn it on. Simulation evaluates existing+new SharePoint/OneDrive items but only *new* items for Exchange, Teams and devices; data kept 30 days. *Stop processing more rules* doesn't work in simulation.
- Teams DLP covers chat and channel messages and shared files; changes take about an hour to sync.
- Power BI/Fabric DLP uses the *Fabric and Power BI workspaces* location (custom policy only, no admin units). Microsoft 365 Copilot location can stop Copilot from processing labeled content.

### Endpoint DLP
- Requirements: Windows 10 x64 1809+ / Windows 11 / Windows Server 2019+ (enable server support), macOS (three latest versions); appropriate licensing (E5-level information protection & governance).
- **Onboarding**: devices already onboarded to **Defender for Endpoint are automatically onboarded**; otherwise Purview portal > Settings > Device onboarding (script, GPO, Intune, ConfigMgr). Device proxy must allow the DLP service; `MpDlpService.exe` must not be blocked.
- **Endpoint DLP settings**: file path exclusions, restricted apps and app groups, unallowed browsers, service domains (allow/block upload sites), printer groups, removable USB device groups, network share coverage, evidence collection, browser/paste restrictions; **Purview extension for Chrome/Firefox**; **just-in-time protection**.

### Reviewing results
- **DLP Alerts** (Purview DLP > Alerts, and incidents in Defender XDR), **Activity explorer** (DLPRuleMatch, file copied to removable media...), DLP **reports** (most triggered rules, top violators), policy simulation dashboards.
- Roles: Compliance Administrator / DLP Compliance Management; alert review via DLP alert roles; Activity explorer viewing needs roles such as Compliance admin, Security admin, Global reader, Security reader, Reports reader.

### Insider risk basics
- Templates: data theft by departing users (HR connector or *user account deleted from Entra* trigger), data leaks (often DLP-triggered), security policy violations (MDE alerts), risky AI usage.
- Privacy by design: users are pseudonymised by default; role groups restrict who sees identities.
modules.architecture:
### DLP evaluation
`Content created/shared -> workload (Exchange transport, SharePoint/OneDrive indexing, Teams message service, endpoint DLP agent in Defender Antivirus) evaluates content against classification (SITs, labels) -> rule match -> action enforced locally + policy tip -> event to unified audit log -> Activity explorer / alerts / Defender XDR incidents`.

Endpoint DLP runs inside the Defender platform on the device (same onboarding as MDE), so classification happens locally and only events/evidence are sent to the cloud.
modules.realWorldExample:
**Scenario - stopping client drawings and personal data leaking**

1. Create a DLP policy from the *GDPR Enhanced* / custom template for Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive and Teams: Belgian national number and IBAN (count >= 5) shared externally -> **block with override** + policy tip; label *Highly Confidential - HR* shared externally -> **block**.
2. Run two weeks in **simulation with policy tips**; the simulation dashboard shows payroll exports sent to the external accountant - add an exception for the accountant's domain.
3. Endpoint DLP: the laptops are already onboarded through Defender for Business, but Endpoint DLP needs E5-level Purview licensing, so the MSP adds *Microsoft 365 E5 Compliance* for the 10 project leads who handle client drawings.
4. Endpoint rule: files labeled *Confidential - Clients* -> **block copy to USB** except company-encrypted USB device group; **audit** uploads to unallowed cloud services.
5. Monthly MSP report from DLP reports: top rules, overrides with justifications, and USB block events.
examTips: Safe rollout order: Keep it off -> simulation -> simulation with policy tips -> Turn it on.
The Allow action exists only for the Devices location; Audit only is the least impactful action elsewhere.
Devices onboarded to Defender for Endpoint are automatically onboarded to Endpoint DLP.
Endpoint DLP supports Windows 10 1809+ x64, Windows 11 and the three latest macOS versions.
Simulation mode evaluates existing SharePoint/OneDrive items but only new items for Exchange, Teams and devices.
Use Activity explorer to see DLP rule matches and label activities.
commonPitfalls: Turning on Block for all locations immediately and stopping payroll or tender submissions.
Forgetting that Endpoint DLP requires appropriate (E5-level) licensing even when devices are onboarded to Defender for Business.
Ignoring proxy configuration for the DLP service on devices.
Over-broad custom SITs causing excessive endpoint classification traffic.
fieldExperience: Overrides with justification are your best tuning data - review them monthly with the customer's data owner.
Policy tips written in the user's language (Dutch/French) dramatically improve acceptance.

questions.stem: A document is subject to an org-wide retention policy (retain 5 years, then delete) and a retention label (retain 10 years). Which TWO principles of retention determine that it is kept for 10 years?

options.text: Retention wins over deletion
The longest retention period wins
The shortest retention period wins
A retention policy's delete action always overrides a retention label
Only the most recently applied setting counts

questions.stem: Your custom sensitive information type uses the regex ^IB-[0-9]{4}$ and never matches project numbers inside documents, although the pattern looks correct. What should you change?

options.text: Remove the ^ and $ positional anchors from the regular expression
Change the confidence level from High to Low
Convert the regex to a keyword dictionary

flashcards.front: Three ways to verify domain ownership in Microsoft 365?
flashcards.back: TXT record (MS=ms...), MX record with a high priority number, or a text file uploaded to the website root.

flashcards.front: Which Microsoft 365 DNS record routes inbound email to Exchange Online Protection?
flashcards.back: The MX record pointing to <domain-with-dashes>.mail.protection.outlook.com.

flashcards.front: Where are planned maintenance and upcoming feature changes announced?
flashcards.back: Message center (Health > Message center), not Service health.

flashcards.front: Does a shared mailbox need a licence?
flashcards.back: Not for normal use within the size limit; licence it only for extra storage, archive or holds.

flashcards.front: Group-based licensing limitation with nested groups?
flashcards.back: Not supported - only direct (first-level) members of the licensed group receive licences.

flashcards.front: Where do you set the update channel for users who self-install Microsoft 365 Apps from Office.com?
flashcards.back: admin center > Settings > Org settings > Services > Microsoft 365 installation options.

flashcards.front: How is Microsoft 365 Backup licensed?
flashcards.back: Pay-as-you-go per GB of protected content, billed through a linked Azure subscription (resource group + region).

flashcards.front: Which role configures office locations in Network connectivity?
flashcards.back: Service Support Administrator (Report Reader can view).

flashcards.front: Microsoft's recommendation for the number of Global Administrators?
flashcards.back: Fewer than five, plus two cloud-only emergency access accounts permanently assigned GA.

flashcards.front: Adding a group to an administrative unit - are its members in scope?
flashcards.back: No. Only the group object is in scope; add users directly (or via dynamic rules) to manage them.

flashcards.front: What licence does PIM require and for whom?
flashcards.back: Entra ID P2 or Entra ID Governance for eligible users, approvers and access reviewers.

flashcards.front: PIM approval window and can it be changed?
flashcards.back: Approvers have 24 hours; the window isn't configurable. Approvers can't approve their own request.

flashcards.front: What does IdFix do?
flashcards.back: Finds and fixes duplicate/invalid values (proxyAddresses, UPN, mail, displayName...) in on-prem AD before sync.

flashcards.front: Default Microsoft Entra Connect Sync cycle interval?
flashcards.back: Every 30 minutes; force with Start-ADSyncSyncCycle -PolicyType Delta.

flashcards.front: Name three reasons to pick Cloud Sync over Connect Sync.
flashcards.back: Disconnected forests (M&A), multiple active agents for HA, lightweight agents with configuration in the cloud.

flashcards.front: Name two reasons you still need Connect Sync.
flashcards.back: Device sync / hybrid join, advanced sync rules, PTA/AD FS configuration, >150K objects per domain.

flashcards.front: Does PTA fail over to PHS automatically?
flashcards.back: No. Enable PHS as backup and switch the sign-in method manually; deploy multiple PTA agents.

flashcards.front: Why enable PHS even with federation or PTA?
flashcards.back: Leaked credentials detection (ID Protection) and disaster recovery if on-prem auth fails.

flashcards.front: Accidental delete threshold default in Connect Sync?
flashcards.back: 500 deletions; exports stop and Connect Health alerts.

flashcards.front: Where do you enable SSPR password writeback in Entra?
flashcards.back: Entra ID > Password reset > On-premises integration (plus writeback in Connect Sync or Cloud Sync).

flashcards.front: Custom banned password list limits?
flashcards.back: Up to 1,000 terms, 4-16 characters each, case-insensitive with substitution handling.

flashcards.front: Can security defaults and Conditional Access policies run together?
flashcards.back: No - disable security defaults to enable Conditional Access policies.

flashcards.front: Sign-in risk vs user risk remediation?
flashcards.back: Sign-in risk -> require MFA. User risk -> secure password change/risk remediation. Keep them in separate policies; needs Entra ID P2.

flashcards.front: Which accounts/roles should be excluded from blocking CA policies?
flashcards.back: Emergency access (break-glass) accounts and the Directory Synchronization Accounts role; service accounts -> workload identities.

flashcards.front: What is a Defender XDR incident?
flashcards.back: A correlated set of alerts and evidence representing one attack across identities, endpoints, email and apps.

flashcards.front: Advanced hunting data range?
flashcards.back: 30 days of raw Defender XDR data (longer only via Microsoft Sentinel).

flashcards.front: Which Secure Score status gives points without implementing the Microsoft control?
flashcards.back: Resolved through third party or Resolved through alternate mitigation. Risk accepted gives 0 points.

flashcards.front: Maximum points per Secure Score recommended action?
flashcards.back: 10 points or less; some actions award partial points.

flashcards.front: Three preset security policy profiles in MDO?
flashcards.back: Standard, Strict, Built-in protection.

flashcards.front: MDO policy precedence?
flashcards.back: Strict > Standard > evaluation > custom (priority) > Built-in protection/default.

flashcards.front: What does Safe Attachments Dynamic Delivery do?
flashcards.back: Delivers the email body immediately with attachment placeholders until scanning completes.

flashcards.front: What does Safe Links add beyond mail-flow scanning?
flashcards.back: Time-of-click verification of URLs in email, Teams and Office apps.

flashcards.front: NDR for a user restricted due to outbound spam?
flashcards.back: 550 5.1.8 Access denied, bad outbound sender.

flashcards.front: Licence for Attack simulation training?
flashcards.back: Microsoft 365 E5 or Defender for Office 365 Plan 2.

flashcards.front: Steps to onboard Intune devices to MDE?
flashcards.back: Defender: Advanced features > Intune connection On; Intune: EDR policy 'Auto from connector'; validate with detection test.

flashcards.front: How do unsanctioned MDCA apps get blocked on devices?
flashcards.back: MDCA syncs indicators to MDE; network protection blocks the domains (up to ~3 hours).

flashcards.front: Exposure score: higher or lower is better?
flashcards.back: Lower. Secure Score for Devices: higher is better.

flashcards.front: What does Business Premium include for endpoints and email?
flashcards.back: Defender for Business (MDE P1 + some P2 features) and Defender for Office 365 Plan 1.

flashcards.front: Why don't users see newly created sensitivity labels?
flashcards.back: Labels must be published in a label policy; allow up to 24 hours.

flashcards.front: Retention policy vs retention label?
flashcards.back: Policy = container level (mailboxes, sites, Teams). Label = item level, one label per item.

flashcards.front: Four principles of retention?
flashcards.back: Retention wins over deletion; longest retention wins; explicit beats implicit for deletion; shortest deletion wins.

flashcards.front: Building blocks of a custom SIT pattern?
flashcards.back: Primary element (regex, keyword list, dictionary, function), supporting elements, proximity, confidence level.

flashcards.front: Safe DLP rollout states?
flashcards.back: Keep it off -> simulation -> simulation with policy tips -> Turn it on.

flashcards.front: How are devices onboarded to Endpoint DLP if MDE is deployed?
flashcards.back: Automatically - onboarding is shared with Defender for Endpoint.

flashcards.front: Content explorer role groups?
flashcards.back: Content Explorer List viewer (items/locations) and Content Explorer Content viewer (item contents).

labs.title: Add and verify a custom domain with all Microsoft 365 DNS records
labs.objective: Add a custom domain to a lab tenant, verify ownership with a TXT record, publish MX, Autodiscover, SPF, DKIM and DMARC records, and make it the default domain.
requirements: A Microsoft 365 E5 trial or Microsoft 365 developer/sandbox tenant (never a customer production tenant)
A test domain you own with access to its DNS zone (e.g. a cheap .be or .eu domain used only for labs)
Global Administrator or Domain Name Administrator in the lab tenant; Exchange Administrator / Security Administrator for DKIM
A DNS lookup tool (nslookup/Resolve-DnsName or an online DNS checker)

steps.title: Start the domain wizard
steps.instructions: Sign in to **https://admin.microsoft.com** > **Settings > Domains > + Add domain**. Enter your lab domain (e.g. `lab-ingbureau.be`) and select **Use this domain**.

steps.title: Choose verification method
steps.instructions: Select **Add a TXT record to the domain's DNS records** and **Continue**. Copy the value `MS=msXXXXXXXX`.

steps.title: Create the TXT record
steps.instructions: At your DNS host create a TXT record: Host `@`, Value `MS=msXXXXXXXX`, TTL 3600. Wait a few minutes and check with `Resolve-DnsName lab-ingbureau.be -Type TXT`.

steps.title: Verify
steps.instructions: Back in the wizard select **Verify**. If it fails, wait for propagation (can take up to 48 hours at some registrars) and retry.

steps.title: Add service records
steps.instructions:
Choose **Add your own DNS records**. Create:
- **MX** `@` -> `lab-ingbureau-be.mail.protection.outlook.com` priority 0
- **CNAME** `autodiscover` -> `autodiscover.outlook.com`
- **TXT** `@` -> `v=spf1 include:spf.protection.outlook.com -all` (merge with any existing SPF record - only one SPF TXT allowed)
Expand **Advanced options** to see optional records. Select **Continue** until *Domain setup is complete*.

steps.title: Enable DKIM
steps.instructions: Go to **https://security.microsoft.com > Email & collaboration > Policies & rules > Threat policies > Email authentication settings > DKIM**. Select the domain, copy the two CNAME values (`selector1._domainkey`, `selector2._domainkey`), publish them at the DNS host, then toggle **Sign messages for this domain with DKIM signatures** to Enabled.

steps.title: Publish DMARC
steps.instructions: Create TXT `_dmarc` with value `v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc-reports@lab-ingbureau.be`. Plan to move to `p=quarantine` / `p=reject` after monitoring.

steps.title: Set default domain and create a test user
steps.instructions: In **Settings > Domains** select the domain > **Set as default**. In **Users > Active users > Add a user**, create `test.user@lab-ingbureau.be` with a licence.

steps.title: Remove the verification record
steps.instructions: Optionally delete the `MS=ms...` TXT record - it's only needed for verification.

validation: Settings > Domains shows the domain with status *Healthy*.
`Resolve-DnsName lab-ingbureau.be -Type MX` returns the mail.protection.outlook.com host.
A test email from an external mailbox arrives in test.user's mailbox; message headers show `dkim=pass` and `spf=pass` for outbound mail.
New users default to the custom domain suffix.
troubleshooting: Verification fails: check that the record is on the apex (@) host and not `@.domain.tld`; some DNS managers append the domain automatically.
Domain shows 'Possible service issues': open the domain and use **Check DNS** to see which record is missing or wrong.
SPF permerror: you have two SPF TXT records - merge them into one.
DKIM toggle fails: CNAMEs not yet propagated or underscores stripped by the DNS host.
cleanup: Reset the default domain to the onmicrosoft.com domain.
Remove users and groups that use the domain (or change their UPN), then **Settings > Domains > Remove**.
Delete MX, Autodiscover, SPF, DKIM and DMARC records at the DNS host.

labs.title: Deploy Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync with password hash sync and SSPR writeback
labs.objective: Prepare a lab AD with IdFix, install the Microsoft Entra provisioning agent, create a Cloud Sync configuration scoped to one OU, and enable SSPR with password writeback.
requirements: A Microsoft 365 E5 trial or Microsoft 365 developer/sandbox tenant (never a customer production tenant) with a verified custom domain (see ms102-lab-domain-dns)
A lab Windows Server 2022/2025 domain controller (e.g. Azure VM or Hyper-V) and optionally a second member server for a second agent
Domain Administrator credentials (to create the gMSA) and a Microsoft Entra Hybrid Identity Administrator account (not a guest)
Outbound HTTPS from the server to Microsoft Entra endpoints
Entra ID P1 or higher licences for SSPR writeback (included in E5 trial)

steps.title: Prepare AD
steps.instructions: Create OU `Sync-Users` with 5 test users. Add the UPN suffix matching your verified domain in **Active Directory Domains and Trusts > Properties > Alternative UPN suffixes** and set it on the test users.

steps.title: Run IdFix
steps.instructions: Download IdFix from Microsoft's GitHub repository, run it against the domain, review **Duplicate**, **Format** and **Blank** errors, apply fixes for the test users and re-run until clean.

steps.title: Download the agent
steps.instructions: In **https://entra.microsoft.com > Entra ID > Entra Connect > Cloud sync > Agent**, select **Download on-premises agent** > **Accept terms & download**.

steps.title: Install the agent
steps.instructions: Run `AADConnectProvisioningAgentSetup.exe`, choose **HR-driven provisioning / Microsoft Entra Connect cloud sync**, sign in as Hybrid Identity Administrator, select **Create gMSA** (supply Domain Admin credentials), add your AD domain, and **Confirm**.

steps.title: Optional: second agent
steps.instructions: Repeat the installation on a second server for high availability (Microsoft recommends three active agents in production).

steps.title: Create the configuration
steps.instructions: In **Cloud sync > Configurations > New configuration > AD to Microsoft Entra ID sync**, select the domain, keep **Enable password hash sync** checked and create.

steps.title: Scope to the OU
steps.instructions: In the configuration, open **Scoping filters** and select **Selected organizational units** = `Sync-Users`. Save.

steps.title: Test with Provision on demand
steps.instructions: Use **Provision on demand** with one test user's DN and review the import, scoping, matching and export steps. Then **Enable** the configuration.

steps.title: Enable writeback
steps.instructions: In the configuration properties enable **Password writeback**. Then go to **Entra ID > Password reset > On-premises integration**, check **Enable password write back for synced users** and **Write back passwords with Microsoft Entra Connect cloud sync**, set **Allow users to unlock accounts without resetting their password** to Yes, and save.

steps.title: Enable SSPR
steps.instructions: In **Entra ID > Password reset > Properties**, set SSPR to **Selected** (a group containing the test users); under **Authentication methods** require 1 method for the lab.

steps.title: Test
steps.instructions: Sign in at https://aka.ms/sspr as a synced user, reset the password, then log on to a domain-joined machine (or use `runas`) with the new password.

validation: Synced users appear in **Entra ID > Users** with *On-premises sync enabled = Yes* and the custom domain UPN.
Cloud sync **Agent** page shows the agent(s) as *Active*.
Provisioning logs show successful *Create* events for the scoped users.
A password reset at aka.ms/sspr works for on-premises logon (writeback succeeded).
troubleshooting: Users land with @tenant.onmicrosoft.com: UPN suffix not set or domain not verified.
Agent install fails: Windows Credential Manager service (VaultSvc) disabled, or TLS/proxy blocks outbound traffic.
PHS errors on first run are expected until users are provisioned; wait a couple of cycles.
Writeback errors: check gMSA permissions and the **Minimum password age** GPO (set 0 for lab).
cleanup: Disable and delete the Cloud Sync configuration.
Uninstall the Microsoft Entra provisioning agent and remove the gMSA if not reused.
Delete synced users in Entra ID (after disabling sync they become soft-deleted or can be converted) and the lab OU.
Turn off SSPR writeback in Password reset > On-premises integration.

labs.title: Conditional Access baseline with report-only mode and break-glass accounts
labs.objective: Replace security defaults with a Conditional Access baseline (block legacy auth, MFA for admins and all users, secure MFA registration) using emergency access exclusions and report-only validation.
requirements: A Microsoft 365 E5 trial or Microsoft 365 developer/sandbox tenant (never a customer production tenant)
Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2 (included in E5 trial)
Conditional Access Administrator (and User Administrator to create break-glass accounts) - use Global Administrator only for the break-glass setup
Two test users registered for Microsoft Authenticator; a FIDO2 key is optional for the break-glass account

steps.title: Create break-glass accounts
steps.instructions: In **https://entra.microsoft.com > Entra ID > Users > New user**, create `bg01@<tenant>.onmicrosoft.com` and `bg02@...` (cloud-only), assign **Global Administrator** permanently, use long random passwords or FIDO2 keys and store them offline.

steps.title: Create exclusion group
steps.instructions: Create security group `CA-Exclude-EmergencyAccess` with bg01 and bg02 as members.

steps.title: Policy 1 - Block legacy authentication
steps.instructions: **Entra ID > Conditional Access > Policies > New policy** (or *Create new policy from templates*). Users: All users, exclude `CA-Exclude-EmergencyAccess`. Target resources: All resources. Conditions > Client apps: **Exchange ActiveSync clients** + **Other clients**. Grant: **Block**. Enable policy: **Report-only**.

steps.title: Policy 2 - MFA for admins
steps.instructions: Users: Directory roles (Global Administrator, Privileged Role Administrator, Security Administrator, Exchange/SharePoint/User Administrator...), exclude the group. All resources. Grant: **Require authentication strength > Phishing-resistant MFA** (or Multifactor authentication for the lab). **Report-only**.

steps.title: Policy 3 - MFA for all users
steps.instructions: Users: All users; exclude the group and the **Directory Synchronization Accounts** role. All resources. Grant: **Require multifactor authentication**. **Report-only**.

steps.title: Policy 4 - Secure security info registration
steps.instructions: Users: All users (exclude group, guests optional). Target: **User actions > Register security information**. Conditions: Locations Any, exclude a named location for your office IP (create under **Named locations**). Grant: Require MFA (users can use Temporary Access Pass). **Report-only**.

steps.title: Validate impact
steps.instructions: Sign in as test users. Review **Sign-in logs > Report-only** tab and **Conditional Access > Insights and reporting** workbook. Use **What If** with a test user, app Office 365 and client app 'Other clients' to confirm policy 1 would block.

steps.title: Cut over
steps.instructions: In **Entra ID > Overview > Properties > Manage security defaults**, set **Disabled** (reason: using Conditional Access). Immediately switch policies 1-4 from Report-only to **On**.

steps.title: Test break-glass
steps.instructions: In a private browser sign in as bg01 and confirm access to the Entra admin center; then configure an alert (e.g. Log Analytics/Sentinel or Defender for Cloud Apps activity policy) for any sign-in by the break-glass accounts.

validation: Sign-in logs show policies *Success*/*Failure* as expected and break-glass sign-ins show the policies as *Not applied*.
A legacy IMAP/SMTP AUTH test (e.g. with a PowerShell Send-MailMessage using basic auth) is blocked.
Test users are prompted for MFA; admins are prompted with the required authentication strength.
Security defaults show Disabled and no users are locked out.
troubleshooting: 'You can't enable this policy while security defaults is on' - disable security defaults first.
Users not prompted: check the user isn't in the exclusion group and that a session already satisfied MFA.
Sync account failing: ensure the Directory Synchronization Accounts role is excluded.
Use the What If tool and the sign-in log Conditional Access tab to see which policy applied.
cleanup: Set lab policies to Off or delete them (keep break-glass accounts if the tenant stays in use).
Re-enable security defaults if no CA policies remain.
Delete named locations and the exclusion group created for the lab.

labs.title: Privileged Identity Management for the Global Administrator role
labs.objective: Convert a standing Global Administrator assignment to an eligible PIM assignment with MFA, justification, a 2-hour activation limit and approval, then test activation and approval.
requirements: A Microsoft 365 E5 trial or Microsoft 365 developer/sandbox tenant (never a customer production tenant)
Microsoft Entra ID P2 or Microsoft Entra ID Governance licences for the eligible user and the approver (E5 trial includes P2)
Privileged Role Administrator (or Global Administrator) to configure PIM
Two test admin accounts (Admin-A eligible, Approver-B) registered for MFA, plus active break-glass accounts

steps.title: Open PIM
steps.instructions: Sign in to **https://entra.microsoft.com** as Privileged Role Administrator > **ID Governance > Privileged Identity Management > Microsoft Entra roles > Roles** and select **Global Administrator**.

steps.title: Configure role settings
steps.instructions: Select **Role settings > Edit**. Activation: max duration **2 hours**, **On activation, require: Azure MFA** (or a Conditional Access authentication context), **Require justification**, **Require ticket information**, **Require approval to activate** with approver **Approver-B**.

steps.title: Assignment settings
steps.instructions: On the **Assignment** tab: do not allow permanent eligible assignments (expire after 6 months); do not allow permanent active assignments (expire after 15 days); require MFA and justification on active assignment.

steps.title: Notifications
steps.instructions: On **Notification** add the MSP security mailbox as additional recipient for role activation alerts. Select **Update**.

steps.title: Create eligible assignment
steps.instructions: Back on the role select **Add assignments**, choose **Admin-A**, assignment type **Eligible**, set the end date, and **Assign**.

steps.title: Remove standing access
steps.instructions: Under **Assignments > Active assignments**, remove any permanent Global Administrator assignment for Admin-A (keep only the two break-glass accounts active).

steps.title: Activate
steps.instructions: Sign in as **Admin-A** > PIM > **My roles > Eligible assignments > Activate** on Global Administrator. Complete MFA, enter justification and ticket number, and submit.

steps.title: Approve
steps.instructions: Sign in as **Approver-B** > PIM > **Approve requests**, select the request, enter justification and **Approve** (within 24 hours).

steps.title: Verify and audit
steps.instructions: As Admin-A refresh **My roles > Active assignments**; open the Microsoft 365 admin center to confirm GA rights. Review **PIM > Microsoft Entra roles > Resource audit / My audit** for the activation and approval events.

validation: Admin-A has no GA rights before activation and full rights after approval.
Activation expires automatically after 2 hours.
Audit history shows request, approval and expiry events; notification email received.
Only the break-glass accounts remain permanently active Global Administrators.
troubleshooting: PIM blade asks for licence: assign Entra ID P2 to the eligible user and approver.
Approver doesn't see requests: verify the approver is configured in role settings; approvers can't approve their own requests.
Activation succeeded but admin center says access denied: sign out/in or wait a few minutes for token refresh.
Lockout risk: never make all GA/Privileged Role Administrators eligible-with-approval without active break-glass accounts.
cleanup: Remove Admin-A's eligible assignment and reset role settings if the tenant will be reused.
Keep break-glass accounts documented or remove them if the lab tenant is decommissioned.

labs.title: Defender for Office 365 preset security policies, Safe Links verification and restricted users
labs.objective: Turn on Standard and Strict preset security policies with impersonation protection, inspect Built-in protection, verify effective policies with PowerShell, and review the restricted entities and alert policy configuration.
requirements: A Microsoft 365 E5 trial or Microsoft 365 developer/sandbox tenant (never a customer production tenant) (E5 includes Defender for Office 365 Plan 2)
Security Administrator role (or Organization Management in Exchange Online)
Exchange Online PowerShell module (Connect-ExchangeOnline)
Two licensed test mailboxes (one 'executive', one regular user) and an external mailbox for tests

steps.title: Open preset policies
steps.instructions: Go to **https://security.microsoft.com > Email & collaboration > Policies & rules > Threat policies > Preset security policies** (or https://security.microsoft.com/presetSecurityPolicies).

steps.title: Configure Standard
steps.instructions: Toggle **Standard protection** On > **Manage protection settings**. *Apply Exchange Online Protection*: **All recipients**. *Apply Defender for Office 365 protection*: **All recipients**. *Impersonation protection*: add the CEO address and the domains of two key suppliers; add trusted senders if needed. **Confirm**.

steps.title: Configure Strict
steps.instructions: Toggle **Strict protection** On > **Manage protection settings**. Apply EOP and MDO protection to **Specific recipients** = the executive test user. Add the same impersonation entries. **Confirm**.

steps.title: Review Built-in protection
steps.instructions: Open **Built-in protection** and note that it applies to all recipients by default; add an exception only for a lab 'security analysis' mailbox.

steps.title: Verify with PowerShell
steps.instructions: `Connect-ExchangeOnline`, then run `Get-EOPProtectionPolicyRule -Identity "Strict Preset Security Policy"`, `Get-ATPProtectionPolicyRule -Identity "Standard Preset Security Policy"` and `Get-ATPBuiltInProtectionRule` to confirm state and scope.

steps.title: Check precedence in the portal
steps.instructions: Open **Threat policies > Anti-spam**: the preset policies appear above custom policies. Create a custom anti-spam policy for the executive and observe that Strict still wins.

steps.title: Test Safe Links
steps.instructions: From the external mailbox send a mail with a link to a harmless site to the regular user. Open it in Outlook on the web and hover the link to confirm Safe Links scanning; review **Reports > Email & collaboration > Threat protection status**.

steps.title: Review alert policies
steps.instructions: Open **Email & collaboration > Policies & rules > Alert policy** and set the recipients of **User restricted from sending email** and **Creation of forwarding/redirect rule** to your lab admin mailbox.

steps.title: Explore restricted entities
steps.instructions: Open **Email & collaboration > Review > Restricted entities** (https://security.microsoft.com/restrictedentities) and run `Get-BlockedSenderAddress` - document the unblock procedure (secure account first, then **Unblock** or `Remove-BlockedSenderAddress`).

validation: Preset security policies page shows Standard and Strict as **On** with the expected recipients.
PowerShell rules show State = Enabled and the correct SentTo/SentToMemberOf conditions.
Message headers/Threat protection status show Safe Links processing for the test message.
Alert policy recipients updated.
troubleshooting: Presets not available: tenant lacks Defender for Office 365; only EOP protections apply.
Users still get custom policy behaviour: confirm they're in the preset scope; presets override custom policies.
PowerShell rule not found: the Standard/Strict rules exist only after the preset was turned on once.
Changes can take a short time to apply; retest after a few minutes.
cleanup: Turn off Strict and Standard presets (or leave on if the tenant remains in use).
Delete custom anti-spam policies and remove Built-in protection exceptions created for the lab.

labs.title: Sensitivity labels, a custom SIT and a DLP policy in simulation mode
labs.objective: Create a custom sensitive information type, create and publish sensitivity labels, and deploy a DLP policy for Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive and Teams using simulation mode before enforcement.
requirements: A Microsoft 365 E5 trial or Microsoft 365 developer/sandbox tenant (never a customer production tenant) (E5 includes Purview information protection, DLP and the explorers)
Compliance Administrator (or Information Protection Admin + DLP Compliance Management) role
Content Explorer List viewer / Content viewer role groups to review results
Two test users with Microsoft 365 Apps (web is sufficient) and an external mailbox

steps.title: Create a custom SIT
steps.instructions: In **https://purview.microsoft.com > Information Protection > Classifiers > Sensitive info types > Create sensitive info type**: name *IB Project Number*; pattern High confidence: primary element regex `IB-[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{3}` (no ^/$ anchors), supporting keyword list `project, werf, chantier` within 300 characters; Medium confidence: regex only. Save and use **Test** with a sample document.

steps.title: Create labels
steps.instructions: **Information Protection > Sensitivity labels > Create a label**: *General* (no protection), *Confidential* (footer 'Confidential - Ingbureau', watermark), *Highly Confidential* with sublabel *HR* (encryption: assign permissions now - HR group Co-Owner). Scope: Files & other data assets, Emails.

steps.title: Order labels
steps.instructions: Confirm label priority: General < Confidential < Highly Confidential (higher order = more sensitive).

steps.title: Publish labels
steps.instructions: **Information Protection > Publishing policies > Publish label**: add the labels (include parent of sublabel), admin units = Full directory, users = a pilot group, policy settings: **Default label for documents = General**, **Require justification to remove or lower a label**, help link to your lab intranet. Name *Pilot label policy* and submit.

steps.title: Create DLP policy
steps.instructions: **Solutions > Data loss prevention > Policies > Create policy** > *Custom* > *Custom policy*. Name *DLP-Project-and-HR*. Locations: Exchange email, SharePoint sites, OneDrive accounts, Teams chat and channel messages.

steps.title: Rule 1 - project numbers
steps.instructions: Create advanced rule: Content contains **IB Project Number** (High confidence, instance count 1+) AND content is shared **with people outside my organization**. Action: **Restrict access** > block only people outside your organization; user notifications with a policy tip; **allow override with business justification**. Incident report: severity Medium, send alert to admin.

steps.title: Rule 2 - HR label
steps.instructions: Content contains sensitivity label **Highly Confidential/HR** shared externally -> **Block** (no override); alert High.

steps.title: Simulation mode
steps.instructions: Policy mode: **Run the policy in simulation mode** with **Show policy tips while in simulation mode**. Submit.

steps.title: Generate activity
steps.instructions: Wait for the labels (up to 24 h) and policy (about 1 h) to sync. As a pilot user create a Word document with `IB-2024-117 project`, apply *Confidential*, save to OneDrive and share externally; send an email containing the project number to the external mailbox.

steps.title: Review results
steps.instructions: Open the DLP policy > **View simulation** (overview, items for review, alerts). Check **Activity explorer** for *Label applied* and *DLPRuleMatch* events and **Content explorer** for the custom SIT and label.

steps.title: Enforce
steps.instructions: After tuning, edit the policy and set **Turn it on right away**; re-test that external sharing shows the policy tip and is blocked/overridable as designed.

validation: Pilot users see the labels in Office apps with General applied by default; downgrade asks for justification.
The SIT test finds the project number with High confidence.
Simulation dashboard lists matched items; after enforcement external sharing is restricted and the policy tip appears.
Activity explorer shows label and DLP rule match events.
troubleshooting: Labels missing in apps: policy not published to the user or still replicating (up to 24 h); sign out/in of Office.
SIT doesn't match existing SharePoint files: content must be re-crawled; test with new files.
No DLP matches in simulation for old emails: Exchange is only evaluated for new items during simulation.
Explorers empty: check role group membership (List viewer/Content viewer) and allow time for indexing.
cleanup: Turn off and delete the DLP policy.
Delete the label policy, then delete labels (removing a label from a policy first; deleted labels remain in already-labeled files' metadata).
Delete the custom SIT and test documents/emails.
